articleTitle: A Fast Modeling Method for Large Metallic Periodic Arrays with Variable Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A fast modeling method for metallic periodic arrays with variable parameters is proposed. This method accelerates the solution process by generating a reduced method of moments (MoM) equation using characteristic mode basis functions (CMBF). Additionally, it speeds up the reduced matrix construction process by separating parameters through the empirical interpolation method (EIM). In this paper, the examples of parameter changes in array element size and frequency are presented, with numerical simulations verifying the accuracy and efficiency of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A RF Sensor to Detect Lipohypertrophy of Insulin Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a design of RF sensor to detect lipohypertrophy of insulin injection. The design uses spiral inductors, which enable the sensor to have multiple resonance frequency and sensitivity to near-field effects, thereby detecting lipohypertrophy. This article validates the sensor through pork and phantom testing, providing a new non-invasive method for detecting lipohypertrophy. In pork testing, lipohypertrophy resulted in a decrease of approximately 5.5 dB in the magnitude of the S11 resonant frequency at 3.95 GHz and 5.45 GHz, and a increase of approximately 4 dB in the magnitude of the peak magnitude of the S21 at 3.25 GHz and 3.95 GHz. In phantom testing, lipohypertrophy resulted in a decrease of 2.2-2.7 dB in the magnitude of the S11 resonant frequency at 5.45 GHz and 6 GHz with 20 MHz shift, and a increase of approximately 1 dB in the magnitude of the peak magnitude of the S21 at 3.17 GHz and 3.9 GHz with 100 MHz shift. Experimental studies show that the presence of lipohypertrophy in tissues can be measured by analyzing changes of S parameters.

articleTitle: A Millimeter Wave Chip Package Designed by Mode Suppressing High Impedance Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a high impedance surface package is proposed to suppress the parasitic resonance of the cavity and the surface wave transmission mode. The high impedance surface is embedded in the package lid, which not only suppresses the cavity resonance, but also prevents the surface wave propagating along the lid. It is scalable to higher frequency without limits by mechanical constraints. Finally, by frabricating and verifying a K-band filter, it is shown that the filter under the test has good performance in the work band, while the out-of-band suppression performance of the filter is improved and broadened.

articleTitle: Cellular-Connected UAV: Recent Advances and Future Trends*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: As the application of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) continues to expand, achieving efficient and stable connectivity in integrated air-to-ground communications has become critical. Cellular networks are poised to provide widearea, high-quality, and secure connections to support UAV operations. However, as the altitude increases, the radio environment changes, posing new challenges for using terrestrial cellular networks to connect UAVs in flight. This paper first introduces the unique air-to-ground channel characteristics of cellular-connected UAVs and explores the impact of these characteristics on communication performance. On this basis, we analyze existing methods for optimizing communication performance and interference mitigation techniques. By comparing the effectiveness of different technical approaches, this paper offers several recommendations for improvement and highlights key directions for future research to further enhance the communication capabilities and reliability of cellular-connected UAVs.

articleTitle: Study on Electromagnetic-Thermal Coupling Effects of Frequency Selective Surfaces Using Multi-Physics Field Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) serves as a spatial filter that selectively interacts with electromagnetic waves. As the microwave power emitted by antennas increases, the electromagnetic thermal effects of FSS can no longer be overlooked. This paper investigates the electromagnetic thermal effects of two distinct FSSs with identical transmission characteristics, modeling and analyzing their temperature variations using multi-physics simulation. The findings reveal significant differences in the steady-state temperatures of FSSs with varying structures, as well as a strong positive correlation between temperature and surface electric field intensity.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Reconfigurable Element for Beam-Scanning Transmitarray Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband one-bit reconfigurable circularly polarized transmission element designed for beam-scanning transmitarray antennas (TAs). The transmission element is designed based on the fundamental structure of a magnetoelectric dipole which exhibits a wide bandwidth due to the resonance combination of the electric dipole and magnetic dipole. A receiving magnetoelectric dipole and a transmitting magnetoelectric dipole are integrated to form the proposed receiving-transmitting (R-T) transmission element. The receiving magnetoelectric dipole is a center-fed, linearly polarized magnetoelectric dipole that is soldered with two p-i-n diodes. By electronically controlling the state of the p-i-n diodes, a reconfigurable one-bit transmission phase can be generated. The transmitting magnetoelectric dipole is a circularly polarized magnetoelectric dipole fed by an L-shaped feed probe. To verify the performance of the transmission element, we conducted simulations using HFSS. The simulation results indicate that the transmission bandwidth ranges from 13.0 GHz to 17.8 GHz, achieving a bandwidth of 31.2 % with a transmission amplitude better than -2.0 dB. The proposed transmission element is an ideal candidate for beam-scanning TA design applications.

articleTitle: Single and Multi-Carrier MIMO Transmission in Beamspace Using Single-RF ESPAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Beamspace single-carrier and multi-carrier transmission schemes for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems using single-radio-frequency (RF) electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) antenna are investigated. Single-RF MIMO based on ESPAR antenna has advantages of smaller size, low cost and higher energy efficiency when compared to conventional MIMO antenna. While with mutual coupling and single RF chain, MIMO transmission using ESPAR is conducted in beamspace domain where multiple streams of symbols are mapped onto a set of orthogonal far-field radiation patterns instead of antenna elements. In this work, single-carrier beamspace spatial modulation (SM) as well as generalized SM are studied while for multi-carrier case, SM-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) and OFDM are investigated. By finding the optimal reactive loads of ESPAR, these single and multi-carrier MIMO transmission schemes can be performed by exciting the radiation patterns corresponding to the symbol streams. Simulation example using ESPAR of 5-element uniform circular array for various schemes in frequency-selective channel are provided. It is shown that bit error rate (BER) of the MIMO system using ESPAR with optimized radiation patterns achieves close performance to conventional MIMO systems, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach and its promise in sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication.

articleTitle: A Compact Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna with Series Sequential-Phase Feed Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A compact circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna with Series Sequential-Phase feed network is proposed in this paper. The antenna structure is mainly composed of a square patch, an array of parasitic metal plates symmetrically positioned around the patch, and a series sequential-phase (SP) feed network as feeding structure. A series SP feeding network provides four signals of equal magnitude and quadrature phase for proposed antenna. The parasitic element provides greater freedom for impedance matching of the antenna. The overall size of the antenna is 0.57 λ × 0.57 λ × 0.071 λ (λ is the free-space wavelength at the lowest frequency). The impedance bandwidth for S11 < -10 dB reaches 36.71% (1.49 - 2.16 GHz), and the axial ratio bandwidth for axial ratio < 3 dB reaches 13% (1.58 - 1.80 GHz). The peak gain of the antenna reached 7.56 dBic.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of ULF Electromagnetic Waves Based on the ADI-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The propagation characteristics of ultra-low frequency (ULF) electromagnetic (EM) waves in the ocean and within the ocean-ionosphere waveguide model have been studied. Numerical simulations were conducted using the alternate-direction implicit finite-difference time-domain (ADI-FDTD) method, and the results were compared with those obtained using the traditional finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. The accuracy and efficiency of the ADI-FDTD method were validated through this comparison.

articleTitle: A Satellite Receiving System Demonstration Plat-Formbased on Measured Behavioral Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: During the teaching demonstration of the satellite receiving system, different underlying modules can be selected according to different working states. In order to obtain a more realistic RF response, the receiver link can be built in the simulation software such as Advanced Design System (ADS), and different simulation templates can be selected to obtain the corresponding features. Simulation in ADS requires the trainee to be very familiar with the simulation software, and there is a high threshold for use. In this paper, a satellite receiver simulation platform is developed, which encapsulates ADS at the bottom layer and calls the simulation template and data display interface designed for different RF indicators. For modules with different functions, you can choose from a variety of measurement-based behavioral models from the model library. The use of this platform allows the trainee to focus more on the operating principles of the receiving system and the device selection strategy, rather than on the use of simulation software.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Design of a Fourth Order Differential Filtering Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a fourth-order differential filtering phase shifter which is consisting of a main filter path and a reference filter path. By properly adjusting the passband bandwidth of the main filter, a stable phase function of the proposed phase filtering shifter is achieved. The main filter is a fourth-order generalized Chebyshev filter with two transmission zeros which is consist of microstrip lines and coupled microstrip lines. The key parameters of the proposed filtering phase shifter are determined by the derived formulas. A prototype is designed with a central frequency of 2.4 GHz, a phase shift of 90°, and a fraction bandwidth of 30%. Good agreement is obtained between the circuit simulation results and the full-wave simulation results.

articleTitle: Decouple of a Shared-Radiator Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Consistent Radiation Performances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this article, a shared-radiator cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) is decoupled with consistent radiation performances. Based on the common mode (CM) and differential mode (DM) cancellation method, the impedances of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TE}_{01\delta}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TE}_{01\delta+1}$</tex> modes that correspond to CM and DM, are equaled by mounting a conformal metallic strip at the middle of the cylinder surface. Hence, the electric field is nearly eliminated around the loaded port, resulting in the reduction of mutual coupling. In addition, no matter which port is driven, the excited field possesses translational symmetry and produces consistent radiation performances. The simulated isolation is higher than 22 dB across the impedance bandwidth; The radiation patterns is consistent and the cross-polarization level is lower than -17 dB.

articleTitle: An Outphasing All-Digital Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: All digital transmitter with outphasing (OADT) has been identified as a suitable candidate for massive MIMO systems. However, with the existing phase modulation methods, the OADT performance is subject to the phase resolution (PR). When the PR is limited, the OADT performance degrades vastly. To address this issue, a novel OADT with mapping-based PWM (MPWM) method is proposed, which is called the MPWM-OADT. The phase modulation is realized by a LUT. The architecture of MPWM-OADT and the components are expounded. By the noise analysis model, the optimizations of adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR) and coding efficiency (CE) are discussed. Simulation and experiment results show that the MPWM-OADT has good performance and it is free of PR limitation. Under the same condition, the MPWM-OADT outperforms the OADTs with other phase modulation methods in ACLR and Error Vector Magnitude (EVM). Meanwhile the indicators keep stable when the PR decreases.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Reconfigurable Orbital Angular Momentum Active Folded Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A polarization-reconfigurable, low-profile active folded transmitarray antenna capable of orbital angular mo-mentum (OAM) generation is presented. The proposed antenna consists of an upper active transmissive metasurface (UATM), a lower polarization-conversion reflective metasurface (LPCRM), and an magnetoelectric dipole feed. The UATM is composed of five metallic conductive layers and three dielectric layers, featuring identical top and bottom metallic layers, each inte-grating two positive-intrinsic-negative (PIN) diodes aligned along the x-axis and two PIN diodes along the y-axis. Full-wave simulation results demonstrate the generation of a polarization-reconfigurable OAM beam with mode <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l=+1$</tex>, achieving mode purity of 70% for x-polarization and 72% for y-polarization. Moreover, the overall antenna height is reduced to one-third of the focal length.

articleTitle: A Capacitorless Self-Resonant Antenna for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper designs a kind of capacitorless self-resonant printed spiral antenna (SR-PSC) systems for wireless power transfer (WPT). The highest efficiency of the designed spiral antenna is 68.7% at an operating frequency of 700 MHz for the WPT system. And the frequency band of ~38 MHz is achieved for a transmission efficiency of no less than 50% with 20 mm air gap. The profile is only 60 × 60 mm which means it can be used in the restricted space and can also reduce the cost of adding additional components.

articleTitle: Design of A Flexible RFID Tag Antenna with High Tolerance in Bending States
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Antenna design for flexible Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tags is crucial due to the impact caused by different kinds of deformation in practical scenarios. In this paper, a special design of an antenna including a meandered semi-ring shape dipole and circular dielectric substrate is proposed, aiming to reduce the performance difference between orthometric deformation. After optimization of parameters by simulation, the antenna shows 0.17% frequency shift and 0.13% frequency shift when bending along the horizontal direction and vertical direction respectively, which indicates that this design has great potential to realize the RFID tag free of impact by different deformation.

articleTitle: Slotted Spoof Surface Plasmons for Millimeter Pencil-Beam Generation and Steering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A low-profile approach for pencil-beam generation and steering based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) and periodically arranged slots is proposed in this paper. Stemming from domino plasmons, we initially analyzed the interaction between linear slots array and domino plasmons after designing a domino plasmon waveguide with two standard rectangle waveguide ports. The results reveal the presence of a fan-beam with frequency-controlled scanning properties across an ultrawide band. Notably, the pervasive open stop band (OSB) effect, which typically poses challenges for broadside radiation leaky wave antennas, is thoroughly considered and effectively mitigated through our dual-slot configuration. Furthermore, we proposed a pencil-beam domino plasmon antenna integrated with a two-stage power divider, the pencil-beam emerges from 45 GHz to 65 GHz with mainbeam direction rotates from 205.4° to 131.8°, the peak gain reaches 21.6 dBi and the beam width is around 12.2°x5.6°. As an unprecedented strategy, this work surmounts the bottleneck of 2D-array based on SSPPs by introducing a high-efficiency integrated power-divider. This approach holds promise as a heuristic method for the generation and manipulation of pencil-beams in millimeter wave band.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Low Cross-Polarization Patch Antenna Design for Future 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain, low cross-polarization microstrip patch antenna is designed for future 6G applications. At first, four shorting pins are loaded to the patch antenna, increasing the radiating area through the shunt inductance effect to enhance the gain of the antenna. Meanwhile, introducing two longitudinal slots on the patch surface further improves the gain and reduces cross-polarization. Simulation results show that within the impedance bandwidth from 6.48 to 6.94 GHz, the proposed antenna achieves an efficiency greater than 90%, a gain greater than 10.2 dBi, and a peak gain of 10.88 dBi, which is approximately 3.1 dB higher than that of the conventional antenna. Furthermore, the antenna demonstrates excellent low cross-polarization characteristics, with the H-plane cross-polarization reduced by approximately 13.3 dB compared to the conventional antenna.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Conformal Rectenna with Pattern Complementarity for Leadless Pacemaker
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A dual-band implantable rectenna with pattern complementarity is presented in this work. Biocompatible RO3010 and polyimide material are used as substrates for the design, and a three-dimension structure combining planar and conformal parts is constructed. The planar part is a planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) miniaturized with a meandered line and three arc slots. The conductor arm on the patch is extended in the cylindrical surface by connecting it to the metal branches controlled by PIN diodes on the conformal part. Stable gain variations within 4 dB at 915 MHz and 8 dB at 1.4 GHz are achieved over the whole three-dimension space, by means of various radiation patterns in different states. Power conversion efficiency up to 68% of the proposed rectifier can be achieved at - 10 dBm input power, which is sufficient for low-power implants. The spatial dimensions of the antenna are π x 3.4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>X 10 mm <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>(π x 0.01λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>x 0.01λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>x 0.03λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>,λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> at 915 MHz), which are close to those of a commercially available leadless pacemaker.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Modeling of Frequency-Selective Surfaces with Thermally Thin Boundary Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Thermally thin boundary condition is applied in this paper to model the electromagnetic-thermal effect of frequency selective surfaces with thin metal structures. The thermal simulation entails a 3-D meshing of the metal films, while excessive elements would greatly increase the cost of electromagnetic simulation. We also introduced the domain decomposition method (DDM) to accelerate the computation of large-scale electromagnetic problems. Numerical results are validated on a conformal frequency-selective surface.

articleTitle: Age of Information in Relay-Aided Wireless Body Area Networks With and Without Retransmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: As a vital metric to characterize information fresh- ness, age of information (AoI) holds a significant importance in networks where timing is critical. This paper explores the information freshness for relay-aided wireless body area net- works (WBAN). By analyzing the status update scheme with and without retransmission, the average AoIs for two schemes are examined and evaluated. Numerical simulations show that the effect of retransmission in relaying WBAN is different from the point-to-point (P2P) one. Specifically, the status update with retransmission achieves the lower average AoI in relaying networks but the higher average AoI in P2P networks.

articleTitle: A Switchable Single/Double-Band Active Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a switchable single/doubleband active frequency selective surface (AFSS). By controlling the DC bias state of the PIN diodes in the interleaved AFSS units, flexible control over three distinct frequency responses is achieved, with a simple feeding structure. States 1 and 2 exhibit single-band frequency responses with resonances at 8.97 GHz and 10.75 GHz, respectively, with insertion losses of 0.66 dB and 0.63 dB. State 3 demonstrates a dual-band frequency response with resonances at 9.01 GHz and 10.70 GHz, with insertion losses of 0.66 dB and 0.60 dB, respectively. All states of the AFSS exhibit polarization insensitivity and good angular stability. This structure provides a novel design approach for active frequency selective surfaces.

articleTitle: The Fast Method for Coated Multiscale Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Fast high frequency electromagnetic algorithms are widely used in the calculation of electromagnetic characteristics of multiscale scatterers. The multi-level physical optics (MLPO) method combines the multi-level concept and the high frequency method to realize the fast computation. However, when the structure of the scatterer tends to be complex and its electrical size increases, the MLPO method faces the difficulties of low computational efficiency and high workload. In this work, a multi-level fast physical optics (MLFPO) method for the coated multiscale scatterer is proposed and realizes the accurate and efficient computation. The computational error between MLFPO method and traditional PO method is 1.15dB.

articleTitle: A Reference-Frequency Doubler with Integrated Duty-Cycle Corrector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a reference-frequency doubler integrated with a duty cycle corrector. A mixed-signal structure is used in the duty cycle corrector. The digital logic control module controls the entire duty cycle calibration process to calibrate the duty cycle of the input reference signal to 50%. The proposed duty cycle corrector uses adjustable delay cells, introducing long and short delays for coarse and fine delay adjustments, respectively. It realizes a comprehensive performance in both correction accuracy and correction cycles. And the use of 4 identical adjustable delay cells helps generate the double-frequency signal through an XOR gate. The output doubled signal also has a duty cycle of about 50% in contrast to the conventional frequency doubler that uses separate DCC and XOR, where the duty-cycle of the output doubled signal is too small. This design is implemented in 40nm CMOS process and successfully achieves the capability to regulate the duty cycle of the input signal from 50%±20% to 50%±1.5% within an input frequency range of 40MHz to 70MHz, requiring only 40 to 80 clock cycles for calibration, thus generating a doubled frequency signal. The design is well-suited for application in PLL systems and significantly aids in reducing the output phase noise of the PLL.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Rectangular Patch Antenna with Circular Polarization for Enhanced Biomedical Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a miniaturized rectangular patch antenna with circular polarization, optimized for enhanced biomedical communication. The antenna operates at 2.45 GHz, a frequency commonly used in medical implants and wireless body area networks (WBANs). The design features a unique structure with cut corners and arrow-shaped slots, enhanced using pins to achieve circular polarization and miniaturization. These design elements help improve signal stability and reduce multi-path interference, which is crucial in the complex and dynamic environment of the human body. The compact size of the antenna facilitates easy integration into implantable and wearable devices. Both simulation and experimental results, including tests using pork tissue and silicone gel to simulate human skin, demonstrate the antenna's effectiveness in maintaining low return loss and stable performance under realistic conditions. The proposed antenna offers a robust solution for reliable and efficient communication in biomedical applications, advancing the capabilities of modern healthcare technologies.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a 2-D Electromagnetic Driven Micromirror
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A new type of electromagnetic driven scanning micromirror is designed in this paper. This paper mainly optimizes the structure of the driving electromagnet of the scanning micromirror system. The electromagnet consists of an outer ring magnet and an inner cylinder magnet, which can drive the motion of the two-dimensional scanning micromirror. And Comsol Multiphysics software was used to simulate and analyze the micro mirror, and we obtained the resonant frequency of the micromirror. The resonant frequency of the slow axis was 153.04Hz, and the resonant frequency of the fast axis was 1092.8Hz. The deflection at different frequencies is obtained by simulation. When the micromirror works in quasistatic mode and the driving current is 0.1A, the deflection Angle at 50Hz is 3.5 degrees. When working in resonant state and the driving current is 0.06A, the frequency is 1092.8Hz, the deflection Angle of the micromirror is 6.5 degrees. The deflection angles of two motion modes under different current are obtained, which proves the rationality of the design.

articleTitle: RSRP Prediction In Low Altitude by Deep Learning-Based Method and Geographic Information
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: With the gradual maturation of aircraft technology and the increasing number of drones, communications in low-altitude airspace will become more and more complex. In order to provide high quality low-altitude communication services, path loss or RSRP prediction of the celluar network is a particularly critical step for base station location and network optimization. In this paper, Digital Elevation Map is employed to provide the geospatial information of the path for RSRP prediction. ResMLP as well as MLP network are utilized to perform feature extraction for the two types of data respectively. Then RSRP values are regressed by the concatenated features. The algorithm achieves an RMSE of 2.94 dB for RSRP prediction and reduces the error by 22.6% compared to MLP-only structure.

articleTitle: How to Achieve Large-scale Development in the Low-altitude Economy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The low-altitude economy in China is undergoing rapid development due to the gradual implementation of national policies. This paper elucidates the factors that influence the growth of the low-altitude economy, namely national policies, spatial resources, various infrastructures, and engineering technologies. These interconnected factors necessitate a comprehensive solution rather than several independent solutions. To research into the core issues related to these four factors, a solution known as the low-altitude intelligent Internet of Things is briefly introduced. This innovative low-altitude intelligent system has the potential to revolutionize resource integration, technological innovation, and implementation mechanisms. Both network constructions and technological breakthroughs play equally significant roles in this new low-altitude intelligent system. By depending on this new intelligent system, large-scale development of the low-altitude economy can be achieved. Ultimately, several suggestions aimed at fostering mutual collaboration within the low-altitude industry are presented.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle, Ultra-Broadband, Linear-to-Circular Polarization Conversion Reflectarray Based on Metasurface with RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an ultra-broadband linear-to-circular polarization conversion reflectarray with wide angular stability based on metasurface. The unit cell consist of a leaf-shaped symmetric structure consisting of parallel short truncated lines printed on a grounded dielectric substrate. Numerical analyses show that the reflectarray composed of such units is capable of converting linearly polarized (LP) incident wave into circularly polarized (CP) reflected wave. The y-polarized incident wave is converted into right-hand circularly polarized (RHCP) wave by reflectarray and x-polarized incident wave is converted into left-hand circularly polarized (LHCP) wave. Under normal incidence conditions, the relative bandwidths of the normalized ellipticity and axial ratio (AR) reach 82.7% and 83.2%, respectively, which completely cover the X-band. The reflectarray is stable over wide frequency range even at incidence angle up to 40°. The application in radar cross section (RCS) reduction is also verified, and the results show that the designed unit cell has potential applications in the field of RCS reduction.

articleTitle: Dual-Beam Tensor Impedance Modulation Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we designed a dual-beam tensor impedance surface antenna with dual feed sources. The basic principles of tensor impedance modulation were introduced, and based on these principles, the unit structure and array arrangement were designed. When the two feed sources operate independently, they radiate ±45° polarized beams, respectively. Finally, a prototype antenna was fabricated and tested, with the test results showing good agreement with the simulations.

articleTitle: Decoupled Dual-polarized Base Station Antennas Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the decoupling of 1*2 dual-polarized base station antennas is realized. Decoupling is achieved by feeding one of the antenna units to excite a pair of modes so that their currents cancel each other out on the other antenna unit. Bending the metal arm of the antenna and adding parasitic elements could adjust the electromagnetic coupling between the antennas. The odd and even modes are excited at the same frequency, and finally the decoupling effect is achieved. The simulation results show that the impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 10% (3.32-3.69GHz), the isolation is greater than 26dB, and the two polarization directions have good decoupling effect.

articleTitle: Traffic Scheduling with Injection Time Allocation in Time-Sensitive Networking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) is an emerging technique which can provide deterministic service and real-time communication in Industrial Internet-of- Things (IIOT). Cyclic Queuing and Forwarding (CQF) mechanism in TSN is an efficient time-aware shaper to eliminate uncertain delay or jitter of transmissions. However, the deterministic requirements of IIOT are diverse and thus the traffic scheduling problems are always with high complexity. In this paper, we study the traffic scheduling problem with CQF mechanism and the goal is to maximize the total flows while satisfy the deterministic requirements of each flow. We propose an efficient algorithm to solve the traffic scheduling problem with CQF mechanism. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm compared to the benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: Prediction of Electrical Characteristics of GaAs HEMT Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: TCAD-based simulation takes a long time and involves a huge amount of data, and it is necessary to establish a physical model that conforms to the actual device parameters and working environment to make the simulation results have reference significance. With the continuous development of artificial intelligence, the current neural network model has stronger and stronger prediction ability, and this paper hopes to apply artificial intelligence to the research of semiconductor devices by using the powerful generalization ability and nonlinear fitting ability of neural network models, which can not only solve the problem of slow simulation solution speed of semiconductor devices, but also effectively reduce the research threshold of non-specialists.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Dual-Polarized Time-Share On-Off Bandpass FSS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Coping with the technical demand of radar stealth, a dual-polarized time-share on-off FSS is simulated in this article. Through the adaption of three layers of CLC compound structures and time-sharing control under the operation of switching diodes with dual and independent control, the proposed structure realized the autonomous regulation between transmission and rejection under TE and TM polarization. The optimum and performance of proposed structures are simulated by the full-wave EM simulation software. Simulation results indicate that this structure realized autonomous regulation between four states, i.e., dual-polarized transmission, single-polarized transmission Isingle-polarized rejection, and dual-polarized rejection. The insertion loss of passband less than IdB ranges from 8.5 to 11.5 GHz, and the stopband of transmission coefficient less than 10dB ranges from 7 to 10 GHz. Moreover, results support the fact that proposed structures realized the autonomous regulation between effective transmission and efficient rejection in desired polarizations. Results denote that the proposed dual-polarized time-share on-off FSS in this article is feasible.

articleTitle: Design of a Fractal-Based Ultra-Wideband Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: To address the limitations of traditional antennas in multi-frequency broadband applications, such as restricted bandwidth and large size, this study proposes a novel ultrawideband antenna design based on a third-order hexagonal fractal structure. By employing sophisticated principles of fractal geometry, this design achieves a working bandwidth from 2.37 GHz to 10.7 GHz with a relative bandwidth of 127.4%, significantly surpassing existing technologies. Incorporating Koch fractal concepts to optimize the traditional hexagonal fractal structure, the antenna excels in the S, C, and X bands, offering broader frequency response and enhanced design flexibility. Simulation results validate the performance of this antenna design, demonstrating its potential applications in modern communication systems. Future research will focus on further enhancing the antenna's radiation efficiency and optimizing its radiation pattern.

articleTitle: DC Power Management for Active Phased Array Terminal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A highly intensive active phased array (APA) terminal typically integrates a variety of complex modules on a multi-layer printed circuit board (PCB), including beamformer chips, an up- and down-conversion module, a wave control module, a receiving and transmitting antenna array, and a power supply module. The function of the terminal requires the power supply module to provide a stable output voltage to the remaining modules. In this paper, a power supply system is designed for a vehicle-mounted phased array terminal to step down the +24V external supply to +5V, +3.3V, +2.5V, +1.5V, and +1V.

articleTitle: Decoupling of Broadband Base Station Antennas Based on Microwave Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, aiming at the coupling problem in base station antennas, a broadband microwave absorber working at 3.3-5 GHz is designed. The proposed microwave absorber compactly places two kinds of ring circuits loaded with patch resistors together. This compact placement method allows two ring loops to resonate simultaneously, expanding the bandwidth of the microwave absorber. The absorption rate of this broadband microwave absorber reaches more than 95 % in its working frequency band. To reduce the coupling between the base station antennas, the microwave absorber is applied to the base station antenna in this paper. The microwave absorber can achieve a 10 dB decoupling effect without affecting the overall performance of the antenna and this simulation results verify the feasibility of applying microwave absorber to base station antenna decoupling.

articleTitle: A 24-30 GHz GaAs MMIC Asymmetric SPDT Switch with Integrated Bandpass Filter in RX Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a 24-30 GHz GaAs monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMlC) asymmetric single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch with integrated bandpass filter in receiving (RX) mode is presented. Due to the different requirements for receiving and transmitting (TX) mode in frontend applications, an asymmetric design is adopted. The TX chain utilizes cascaded series-parallel units and stacked transistor stages to increase power handling capacity and ensure isolation. In RX chain design, a filtering design based on multiple transmission paths is integrated into the switch to reduce interference from other frequency bands. The proposed asymmetric filtering SPDT switch is implemented in 0.10-µm GaAs pseudomorphic highelectron mobility transistor (pHEMT) process and demonstrates low insertion loss and high-power handling capabilities. Simulation results show RX mode with a maximum in-band insertion loss of 1.77 dB and good selectivity, while TX mode has a 1.34 dB of maximum insertion loss and IP1dB of more than 37 dBm. The chip's total area is 1.15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, showing a compact size.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Assisted Resonance Response Prediction With Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a machine learning-assisted prediction model with data augmentation (DA-MLAP) is proposed for accurate resonance response prediction. Traditional multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) normally struggle to accurately predict S-parameters in regions close to resonant frequencies due to limited data availability. To address this limitation, the DA-MLAP incorporates interpolation-based data augmentation to enhance the quality and diversity of the training dataset, particularly in resonance regions. Initially, a conventional MLP is employed to establish baseline predictions for the frequency and reflection coefficient (ISn!). Subsequently, an augmented dataset created through interpolation is used for a second prediction phase with the MLP. The effectiveness of the approach is validated by comparing predictions with actual| S11| values. Experiments are conducted using a probe-fed patch antenna and a cross-shaped slot frequency selective surface (FSS). Results indicate that the DA-MLAP significantly improves the prediction accuracy of resonant responses compared to traditional MLPs, offering a reliable method for applications in resonant filter, antenna, and single-layer frequency selective surface design.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Endfire Planar Antenna Based on Magneto-Electric Dipole
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized (CP) endfire planar antenna based on magneto-electric dipole is proposed in this work. The antenna is constructed based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW), where the open-ended SIW operates as magnetic dipole and two metal strips connected with SIW operate as electric dipole. By using C-shaped tapered electric dipoles and etching elliptical notches on both top and bottom surfaces of SIW, the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth can be effectively broadened. Simulated results show that the −10 dB reflection coefficient and 3-dB AR bandwidths of the proposed antenna are 35 GHz ~ 80 GHz and 38.8 GHz ~ 71.1 GHz, respectively. And the simulated peak gain is 8.6 dBi.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on The Indirect Effects of Nearby Lightning Strikes on Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: To study the protective capabilities of aircraft against the indirect effects of nearby lightning strikes. Following standards and test methods such as GJB 8848-2016 and GJB 1389B-2022, a simulation environment was constructed in the CST Microwave Studio using the standard method and the lightning channel model method. Based on the transmission line matrix method, the impact of nearby lightning on aircraft was analyzed, focusing mainly on surface currents, electric and magnetic field distributions on the aircraft body, as well as the internal electromagnetic field and the magnitude of the coupling current in cables. The simulation results show that the outcomes of both methods are largely consistent, and both can effectively simulate the indirect effects of nearby lightning on aircraft.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Broadband Dipole Antenna for Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A dual-polarized broadband dipole antenna designed for base stations is introduced in this paper. The antenna functions within a operates spectrum from 1710MHz to 3600MHz, featuring a bandwidth of 1.89GHz and a peak gain of 10.9dBi. It is composed of a Printed Circuit Board(PCB) microstrip line base, the balun made up by two Γ-shaped feed strips, four square radiating patches with bottom parasitic stubs and an octagonal parasitic patch, extending the bandwidth and increasing the gain. The antenna exhibits a simple structure, excellent performance, low cost, and easy assembly. The proposed radiating element and the phased array base station antenna constructed from it have been mass-produced.

articleTitle: Parallelized Equivalence Principle Algorithm for Multiple PEC Bodies of Revolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Parallelized equivalence principle algorithm (EPA) for multiple PEC bodies of revolution (BoR) is proposed. Due to the introduction of the equivalent spheres (ES), the scattering and translation operators of EPA for Fourier modes can be obtained independently, making the parallel algorithm more efficient. The strategies based on supercomputer architecture for matrix generation and solver are both developed.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective Near-Field Calibration for Uniform Linear Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel near-field calibration method for uniform linear arrays (ULAs) without requiring anechoic chambers. Our approach uses a single near-field source transmitting frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) signals. We propose a joint gradient descent algorithm that simultaneously estimates array error parameters and precisely locates the calibration source, initialized with an approximate source position. The method leverages FMCW signal characteristics to model channel delay and phase errors. Through simulations, we determine optimal signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and iteration requirements. The algorithm's effectiveness is validated on a 64-antenna ULA, demonstrating improved performance in ranging and back-projection imaging applications. This cost-effective technique offers a practical solution for ULA calibration in non-ideal environments, potentially expanding the use of high-precision phased array systems.

articleTitle: A 98-158GHz On-Chip Bondwire Differential Antenna with 2.6dBi Gain and 80% Efficiency for Sub-THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This work proposes a compact on-chip bondwire differential antenna with wide bandwidth and high efficiency for sub-THz applications. To enhance the gain and radiation efficiency by reducing interference with the lossy silicon substrate, a ground plane is introduced to the differential loop antenna. The antenna is shaped to predominantly radiate vertically to the wafer surface. Additionally, a shunt differential bondwire inductor is proposed to broaden the bandwidth. Based on a 65nm bulk CMOS process, the proposed antenna achieves a maximum gain of 2.6dBi, a maximum radiation efficiency of 80%, and a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 47%, showing great potentials compared to the-state-of-the-art on-chip antennas.

articleTitle: High Q Values Non-Uniform PCB Coil for Inductive Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Inductive Power Transfer (IPT) garners significant interest owing to its wireless energy transmission capability. Its transfer efficiency directly correlates with quality factor (Q)values of transceiver coils, and therefore, reducing losses while preserving the self-inductance is vital. As the operating frequency rises to the megahertz (MHz) band, traditional stranded coil is difficult to maintain good performance due to the processing. Rising alternating current (AC) losses makes IPT system turns to PCB coil. However, printed circuit board (PCB) coil's AC losses dominated by proximity effects. To increase the Q values of the PCB coil, this paper proposes a novel coil with non-uniform wire spacing and wire width. Non-uniform wire layout strategy reduces the magnetic induction intensity (B) above the copper traces, thus reducing the eddy current losses. Also wire widths are designed to balance eddy current and conduction losses, resulting in overall losses reduction. Simulations demonstrate 7% AC losses decrease over conventional coils, with a Q value of 464.5, underlining its performance superiority.

articleTitle: A Compact High-Selectivity Bandpass Filter Based on Through-Glass-Via IPD Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This manuscript introduces a miniaturized LC bandpass filter utilizing Through-Glass-Via-based Integrated Passive Device(IPD) technology. The dimensions of the filter are 1.19×0.97 millimeters. The filter is designed to function within the 5G N77 frequency band. It achieves a return loss exceeding 18dB and an insertion loss of less than 1.25 dB within the passband from 3.3GHz to 4.2GHz. The filter employs a dual-mode resonator and is designed with a symmetrical structure for analysis. The filter achieves two transmission zeros at low frequencies and one at high frequencies, thereby suppressing the N41 and WIFI-5G frequency bands.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Dual-Frequency Reflective Metasurfaces Based on Deep Learning and Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel inverse design method integrating deep learning models with multi-objective optimization algorithms to achieve rapid inverse design of metasurface elements. The method enhances the model's forward prediction performance by adopting Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) instead of the traditional Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP). It also employs the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to address the uncertainty issue in non-target frequency bands and the problem of multiple design objectives not being able to simultaneously reach optimality in dual-frequency metasurface element design. Based on this method, A dual-frequency reflectarray antenna we designed achieves symmetric dual-beam and single-beam deflection at the frequencies of 8.0 GHz and 16.5 GHz, respectively. The results demonstrate that this method not only efficiently realizes the on-demand inverse design of dualfrequency metasurface elements but also provides an innovative solution for the design of complex metasurface structures.

articleTitle: High-Performance Surface Acoustic Wave Filters on Heterogeneous Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this talk, a new generation surface acoustic wave (SAW) filter technology on heterogeneous substrates was introduced. Our recent progress in the fabrication of piezoelectric thin films and high-performance SAW devices for 5G and Wi-Fi 6/7 applications were presented.

articleTitle: An Efficient Simulation Method for Self-Heating Effect of GaN HEMTs with Time Scaling Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: To address the issue of low efficiency for electro-thermal coupling in physical modeling, a time scaling factor is proposed to expedite the simulation process of self-heating effects. Firstly, the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) produced by polarization effects, and heterojunction formed by the contact of different semiconductor materials in GaN HEMTs are characterized by continuity conditions. Then, the process of scaling factor acting by electrical and thermal time stepping is introduced. Simulation results show that the proposed method can save 93% computing time and 54% computing memory compared with COMSOL while ensuring accuracy. The self-developed algorithm provides a novel analysis scheme for the electrothermal characterization of devices.

articleTitle: Full Bridge Self-Resonant Synchronous Rectifier for MHz Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Synchronous rectification at several MHz faces a lot of difficulties including signal propagation delay of tens of nanoseconds, the existence of parasitic components, and the significant increase in circuit components and circuit area. These factors limit the wide application of synchronous rectification at the frequency band of MHz. In this work, to partly solve the problem mentioned above, a topology of a full bridge selfresonant synchronous rectifier is proposed. The proposed circuit only contains passive components to maximally reduce the circuit area and generate driving signals through resonance of the passive components to avoid the influence of propagation delay. Experiments are conducted to validate the proposed solution. A full bridge self-resonant synchronous rectifier is built to output 12V/4A with an efficiency of 90.98%. Compared with full bridge rectifier made with the state-of-the-art Schottky Diodes (RBR5LAM40 from ROHM CO., LTD) working under the same conditions, the proposed circuit can reduce the rectification losses by 31.83%.

articleTitle: An Ultrawideband High-Efficiency Rectifier for Wireless Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel rectifier based on voltage multiplier is proposed to operate within ultrawide bandwidth. The ultrawideband rectifier is composed of a voltage multiplier and simple matching network. The matching network is divided into two parts: a section of microstrip radial stub (MRStub ) and a two-section transformer. The MRStub stabilizes the input reactance of sub-rectifier close to zero over an ultrawideband frequency range, and the two-section transformer further tunes the impedance to 50 Ω. The simulated results show that the rectifier can maintain high efficiency over 50% within the frequency range of 0.1 to 6.4 GHz at 20 dBm input power, and the dimension is 29.4mm ×16.5mm, indicating that the proposed structure has the advantages of compact size, ultrawide bandwidth, and high efficiency.

articleTitle: A Q-Band Low Noise Amplifier with 22-Db Gain and Ultralow 5.6-Mw Power Consumption Using GaAspHEMT Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a Q-band ultralow-power pseudomorphit high electron mobility transistor (pHEMT) low noise amplifier (LNA) MMIC. A novel low power technology has been proposed to decrease the DC power consumption of the amplifier. A series of lossy matching circuits have been properly designed to achieve a flat gain in the entire 42-48GHz frequency band. The fabricated LNA exhibits an excellent performance that the DC power consumption is as low as 5.6 mW with an average small-signal gain of 22.1 dB, where the minimum noise figure (NF) is 2.2 dB at 42.4 GHz. It exhibits the lowest power consumption with excellent gain and noise performance, among all Q-band GaAs pHEMT LNAs ever reported.

articleTitle: Space-Air-Ground-Marine-Submarine Integrated Networks Simulation in NS-3
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: As 6G communication systems develop, the Space-Air-Ground-Marine-Submarine Integrated Networks (SAGM-SINs) emerge as a vital framework, addressing the need for comprehensive information services across military, navigation, and IoT sectors. This paper proposes an integrated network model that combines satellite, aerial wireless, and underwater acoustic communications, aiming to surpass the limitations of single communication modes while enhancing their respective strengths and ensuring mutual enhancement. The paper details the model's implementation on the NS-3 platform and assesses the performance of AODV, VBF, and an ModifiedVBF protocol, focusing on delivery ratio and end-to-end delay. It reaches its conclusions through simulation and result analysis, demonstrating the integrated network's capability to optimize communication routes and boost efficiency.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous PMLFMA for Strategies of Accelerating Aggregation Process on DSP Clusters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper, based on domestic supercomputers and combined with the MT3000-digital signal processor (M-DSP), tests the performance of the Method of Parallel Multilevel Fast Multipole Algorithm (PMLFMA) at both coarse-grained process level and fine-grained thread level. Taking DSP platform as an example, a method to accelerate the Aggregation process on CPU-DSP heterogeneous platform is introduced. The test result shows that under the condition of more than 100 million unknowns, the process can be expanded by 20 times while still ensuring more than 30% parallel efficiency.

articleTitle: A 2–6 GHz Wideband Power Amplifier with a Lossy Matching Network in 40-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A wideband power amplifier (PA) with the lossy matching network is presented in this paper. The PA has two amplification stages, the driver stage and the power stage. Thin-oxide type transistors are used in the common-gate configuration of the driver stage, while thick-oxide transistors are adopted in the power stage to provide enough gain. And the neutralization capacitors are used in the driver stage to improve stability and power gain. The output matching network is based on the conventional magnetically coupled resonator (MCR). And the small resistors are connected in series with the secondary inductor in the inter-stage matching network to extend the bandwidth. The designed PA, implemented in 40-nm CMOS technology, operates in 2–6 GHz. It achieves a peak gain of 28.7 dB from 2 to 6 GHz, delivers a saturated output power of 28.7 dBm, and provides a power added efficiency (PAE) of 37.6% at 3.5 GHz. With the fractional bandwidth of 100%, it can be used in various wireless applications.

articleTitle: A Microwave/Millimeter-Wave Dual-Band Shared-Aperture Antenna for S/V-Bands Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a microwave/millimeter-wave dual-band shared-aperture antenna. It is designed based on a transmitarray antenna (TA) operating in the V-band, and the transmitting surface (TS) of the TA is structurally reused as a dipole antenna in the S-band. This study found that due to the large frequency ratio of the two bands, the unit cells (U Cs) of the TS are extremely small in electric size (S-band), and thus the TS can be equivalent to two metal sheets playing roles of dipole arms in the S-band. Benefiting from the spatial feeding architecture of the TA, the proposed antenna eliminates the need of complicated feeding network and features low feeding loss and high gain in the V-band. In addition, because of the efficient integration of the two kinds of antennas, the proposed antenna features a high structure reuse efficiency over the existing studies. The numerical results show that it can achieve −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 47.3% (1.84-2.98 GHz) and 3-dB gain bandwidth of 18.7% (54.8-66.1 GHz), and the peak gain in the S- and V-bands are 8.35 dBi and 28.2 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Hollow-Waveguide-Fed Wideband Terahertz Antenna Array Using Patch Subarray
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This work presents a wideband and high-gain microstrip patch antenna array operating in terahertz frequency range. The array consists of 4 × 2 patch subarrays designed using PCB technology. These subarrays are fed by a hollow waveguide feeding network fabricated through mechanical milling. The proposed array exhibits a wideband impedance bandwidth of 24%, covering a frequency range from 153 to 195 GHz. The highest gain of the proposed array is 21.9 dBi. The proposed array holds great promise for applications in terahertz wireless communications.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous FEM for Analysis of Electromagnetic Scattering on Tianhe Supercomputer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The paper implements the parallelization of the finite element method and deploys it on Tianhe next-generation high-performance supercomputer. Based on edge-based finite element, a Message Passing Interface (MPI) parallel strategy for distributed storage of local matrices is designed. Additionally, a communication strategy is proposed to reduce vector communication volume in the sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) operations involved in iterative solvers.

articleTitle: High Dimensional Uncertainty Quantification in Integrated Micro-System Multiphysics Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In real-world scenarios, the true state of the integrated micro-system is influenced by various uncertainties, rendering it infeasible to assess micro-system performance with deterministic multiphysics modeling alone. Therefore, we propose a high-dimensional uncertainty quantification framework, which describes the multiphysics fields of integrated microsystems from a statistical perspective. Considering the impracticality of intrusive methods due to multiphysics coupling and geometric uncertainties, the proposed method relies solely on data, ensuring its applicability. To address the curse of dimensionality caused by high-dimensional uncertainties, we evaluate the correlation between polynomials and the fields of interest, retaining only significant bases to reduce the required sample size. Numerical experiments demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed algorithm in extracting statistical features, predicting multiphysics field, and analyzing sensitivity.

articleTitle: Model Analysis of Transmission and Computing Resource Optimization for Internet of Vehicles Based on 5G and Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The resource optimization of Internet of Vehicles (IoV) systems based on the integration of 5G and edge computing is one of the key technologies for achieving vehicle-road collaboration and internet-connected autonomous driving applications, which has garnered widespread attention from both academia and industry. This paper initially reviews and summarizes existing research on the optimization of transmission and computing resources in IoV systems based on 5G and Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC). Subsequently, it focuses on optimizing network utilization and the transmission and computing costs associated with task offloading under conditions of high-speed vehicle mobility and limited channel resources. A theoretical framework for the optimization problem and two approximate algorithms are proposed. The research findings presented in this paper contribute to the next phase research on transmission reliability and computing resource utilization of 5G+MEC IoV systems.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Multi-Beam Dual-Polarized Luneburg Lens Antenna for High-Speed Rail Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A dual-band multi-beam dual-polarized Luneburg lens antenna has been proposed for high-speed rail systems. The antenna employs a three-layer Luneburg lens for multi-beam high gain radiation patterns. Two lower-band (LB) antenna and three higher-band (HB) antennas serve as a dual-band feed source of the Luneburg lens. The HB and LB antennas share the same aperture and are conformal to the spherical feed surface. The dual-band multi-beam antenna operates at the lower band of 1.71-2.17 GHz and the higher band of 3.4-3.6 GHz providing three different radiation beams, including two beams for long-range coverage with different azimuth angles and a wide beam for a short-range coverage. This antenna may find potential application in high-speed rail systems for large capacity and wide coverage.

articleTitle: Meta-Fluid Antenna for Multiplexing Multiple Users in Rich Scattering Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: With the rapid development of wireless communication technologies, supporting a massive number of user devices has become a significant challenge. Traditional multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology requires sophisticated signal processing techniques to support a large number of terminal devices in a rich scattering environment. To address this problem, this paper proposes a full-wave simulation model of a meta-fluid antenna that enables multiple devices to access the channel simultaneously, with Rayleigh fading mimicked by artificial rich-scattering generators. This multiple access scheme is referred to as fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA). The FAMA technology enhances system multiplexing efficiency and network performance by allowing user devices to dynamically select optimal receiving positions, thereby maximizing the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR). The proposed method aims to simplify signal processing complexities for terminal devices and eliminate the need for channel state information (CSI) from base stations, thus achieving a larger number of connections and higher data rates by leveraging scattering with low system complexity.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Low-Profile Circularly Polarized Folded Transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In our work, a shared-aperture circularly polarized folded transmitarray (FTA) with ultra-low profile, high gain and high aperture efficiency is proposed for satellite communication systems. A dual-frequency multifunctional metasurface has been designed for operation in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ka}$</tex> bands. It is a receiver-emitter structure comprising circularly polarized receiver patches and circularly polarized transmitter patches. The generation of anomalous reflections at the dual-frequency band is made possible by the use of dual-frequency reflection phase, thereby achieving ultra-low profile.

articleTitle: 3-D Printed Multi-Layer Low-Profile Coupler based on Vertically Integrated CRLH Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper demonstrates several low-profile multilayer electronics fabricated using a novel 3D printing technology. This novel 3D printing technology can fabricate multilayer models with conductive and dielectric materials. In order to reduce the insertion loss and dimension of the electronics, a vertically integrated composite right/left handed (VI-CRLH) transmission line is proposed. And VI-CRLH couplers with good performance are design.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Dual-Polarization Antenna for 2/3/4G and 5G Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A novel ±45° dual-polarized broadband base station antenna for 2/3/4G and 5G applications is presented in this paper. The antenna is composed of a radiator, a parasitic structure, and a metal reflector. Four pairs of dipoles are printed on the upper and bottom layers of the radiator's substrate. The parasitic structure, located above the radiator, can enhance the bandwidth and increase gain in the high frequency range. The antenna is fed through two coaxial cables and two copper pillars. When the return loss is less than -15dB, the relative impedance bandwidth is 73.5% (1.71GHz-3.7 GHz). The antenna gain is 8.3dBi to 10.2dBi and the port isolation greater than 28dB. The antenna offers wide bandwidth, high gain, and excellent port isolation, making it well-suited for base station applications.

articleTitle: Broadband and High Transmission 45-Degree Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A broadband and high transmission 45° polarization converter is proposed in this paper. Based on a simple cavity structure of polarization gate combined with intermediate dielectric plate of variable dielectric constant material, x-polarized incident wave is effectively converted to 45° polarization mode in the frequency range of wideband 13.5GHz-40GHz (relative bandwidth is 99.1%), and the polarization conversion efficiency of more than 85% is achieved.

articleTitle: Active Ultrasensitive Phase Singularities with Bound States in the Continuum
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: We demonstrate that phase singularities, akin to the singularities of BICs in reciprocal space, emerge in dielectric metasurfaces with finite losses. In these systems, losses play a crucial role in achieving the phase singularities within the phase spectra. These phase singularities are robust across parameter space, exhibit sharp phase transitions highly sensitive to external disturbances, and lead to infinite group delays, significantly enhancing sensitivity. By introducing an external pump channel, we can regulate nonradiative losses, thereby actively tuning both the operating conditions and sensitivity of the system. The proposed metasurfaces also improve resonance quality factors through BIC-enabled phase singularities, further enhancing the sensing figure of merit via increased local fields. This active approach to dielectric metasurfaces offers a flexible means of accessing phase singularities, supporting the development of ultrasensitive optoelectronic devices for sensing and detection applications, where the radiative loss channel is governed by BIC physics, and the nonradiative loss channel is modulated by an external pump source.

articleTitle: Loop Closure Detection Method Based on Point Cloud Height Distribution and Contour Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The loop closure detection module, which reduces accumulated error by constructing loops based on whether the robot has previously visited the current scene, is a crucial component in simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). This paper proposes a loop closure detection method based on LiDAR point cloud height distribution and contour features. The point cloud is first downsampled using an adaptive voxel grid filter for efficiency. The point cloud coordinate system is redefined with centroid alignment and principal component analysis (PCA). Height distribution and contour features are encoded into descriptors, and Hamming distance and contour similarities between frames are computed. These similarities are weighted and combined to identify loop closures. Extensive experiments on public datasets validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Dual-Polarized Dual-Band Base Station Antenna Based on AMC Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band dual-polarized aperture shared low-profile base station antenna based on the AMC structure is proposed. The proposed antenna introduces backcavity boxes which can reshape the radiation environment of highfrequency (HF) antenna. The designed AMC structure can offset the phase reflection of the low-frequency (LF) antenna, thus realizing low-profile antenna. The proposed antenna can cover both 0.69-0.96GHz and 3.3-3.9GHz, and realize isolation of more than 70 dB in LF and 25 dB in HF band. The proposed antenna mains stable gain above 7.5 dBi in LF and 7.8 dBi in HF respectively, and the profile of the proposed antenna is 0.145 λL.

articleTitle: 2-D Beamforming with a Terahertz Reconfigurable Transmitarray Using 1-Bit Transparency Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A concise unit cell for terahertz-wave transparency modulation is proposed with a monolithically integrated Schottky barrier diode, achieving an on/off ratio greater than 10 at 215 GHz. Beamforming simulations applied to a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50 \times 50$</tex> transmitarray based on the reconfigurable unit are conducted with a 1-bit transparency modulation method. Operating between 210 and 220 GHz, the transmitarray achieves a beam steering range of up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 70^{\circ}$</tex>, an average gain of 17.75 dB for normal radiations, a gain roll-off of less than 2.02 dB, and a maximum modulation loss of 8.91 dB, under the illumination of an isotropic point source. The proposed reconfigurable transmitarray also demonstrates effective simultaneous multi-beamforming.

articleTitle: A 3.3-4.1 GHz Wideband Doherty Power Amplifier MMIC with Novel Bandwidth Expansion Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel 3.3-4.1 GHz wideband two-stage Doherty power amplifier (DPA) MMIC fabricated in a 250 nm Gallium-Nitride (GaN) MMIC process is presented. In order to break the bandwidth limitation of traditional DPAs, a novel bandwidth expansion technology including the broadband active load modulation network and phase compensation network is proposed. The measurement results show that the fabricated DPA chip can achieve 39.7-40.7 dBm saturation output power (Psat) in the range of 3.3-4.1 GHz.
