The power added efficiency (PAE) at saturation is 45.7%-51.1%, and the PAE of 40.2%-43.80% can be achieved at the output power rollback of 6dB, and the small signal gain is 22.7-26.8 dB. The proposed DPA demonstrates high saturation and 6dB back-off PAE among published C-band wideband GaN DPA MMICs, which can be widely used in the 5G massive MIMO applications.

articleTitle: Effect of Equivariance in Uncertainty Quantification for Full-Wave Inverse Scattering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this work, we compare an equivariance-based uncertainty quantification method with traditional uncertainty quantification methods for solving inverse scattering problem (ISP). By utilizing the equivariance property of certain transformations in ISP, a set of prediction results corresponding to the same input can be obtained and used for uncertainty quantification. By numerous tests, it is shown that uncertainty quantified by the equivariance-based method has significant higher correlation with the true error than the perturbation-based methods, such as Monte Carlo Dropout (MCD). It also achieves comparable performance with Deep-Ensemble, while it needs much less training and storage cost. Furthermore, reasons why equivariance perform well in uncertainty quantification is analyzed.

articleTitle: Decoupling Design of Dual-Band Dual-Polarization Shared-Aperture Antenna for 5G and U6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the new dual-band shared-aperture base station antennas are proposed to solve the current antenna fusion needs of different frequency bands. The proposed antennas consist of a low-band (5G, 3.3-3.7 GHz) antenna and four high-band (U6G, 6.425-7.125 GHz) antennas. Due to the compact distance between the high-band antennas, the coupling between the high-band elements is enhanced, and the low-band antenna will also block the radiation pattern of the high-band antennas. The proposed decoupling structure designed in low-band antenna can effectively solve the above problems. The simulated results show that the isolations between the antenna elements in the high frequency band have been effectively improved, and the radiation patterns in the high frequency band have also been restored.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Bandpass Filter Using Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: An Ultra-Wideband bandpass filter (BPF) using novel circle-shaped defected ground structure (DGS) resonators and inter-digital capacitors is proposed in this paper. The BPF is designed by cascading a novel microstrip highpass filter (HPF) and a lowpass filter (LPF). The LPF with a 3 dB cutoff frequency of 6.1 GHz is constructed by a ladder-shaped transmission line on the top plane and the combined open loop DGS on the bottom one, resulting high selectivity and good stopband performance. The HPF consists of a ladder-shaped transmission line with zigzag slot on the top plane and circle-shaped DGS on the bottom one, providing two transmission zeros and steep rejection slope. The designed BPF with a 3 dB bandwidth of 2.8 GHz and center frequency of 4.7 GHz exhibits wide passband and sharp cutoff frequency response. The BPF also shows good stopband performance with rejection better than 28 dB from DC to 3.1 GHz in lower stopband and with rejection better than 15 dB from 6.3 to 18 GHz in upper stopband, respectively.

articleTitle: Wideband Vertically Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna with low profile for Partial Discharge Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a design method for a patch antenna that achieves a broad bandwidth, good omni-directivity, and a low-profile configuration. The antenna's design leverages a circular patch coupled with four feeding loops to facilitate multi-band resonance, thereby expanding the bandwidth. Following design optimization, the antenna has good impedance matching and maintains excellent omnidirectional performance. The prototype was tested. The antenna has accomplished an ultra-wide bandwidth ranging from 1.65 to 3.26 GHz, alongside maintaining its omnidirectional radiation pattern and a very low profile (0.07 times the free-space wavelength λo at the lower edge of the operational frequency band).

articleTitle: A Filtering Antenna with Low Reflection Characteristics at Band-Edges
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this letter, an absorptive filter antenna is designed for application in the n78 frequency band. The antenna consists of two parts, a reflective filter antenna (RFA) with four filter zeros, and a band-stop filter (BSF) with a stop band containing the n78 band, where a 50-ohm absorptive load is connected to the output of the BSF. The initial design of the patch antenna itself has a low-frequency zero, a low-frequency and a high-frequency zero are created for the antenna by extending the length of the microstrip line of the feed network, and a straight section of open-circuit microstrip line is used to bring a new highfrequency filtering zero to the antenna. Finally, a metal shorting pin is used to connect the inputs of the RFA and the BSF together into a parallel form to realize an antenna that operates with a bandwidth of 14% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(3.3 \text{GHz} \sim 3.8 \text{GHz})$</tex> within the frequency band <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.08 \text{GHz} \sim 3.98 \text{GHz}$</tex>, with a maximum in-band gain of 8.2 dB, and with an overall antenna size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.7 \lambda_0 \times \lambda_0 \times 0.12 \lambda_0 ( >\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the center of the antenna's wavelength at the frequency), an out-of-band rejection level of more than 19.3 dB, and an AFA with high rolloff rate and out-of-band frequency signal absorption performance.

articleTitle: Performance Testing and Verification of 5G-Supported V2X Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: With the continuous and rapid development of intelligent connected vehicles and smart transportation systems, V2X applications are considered by the industry to be the next key direction for evolution. Recently, the use of 5G networks to implement some V2X applications has been increasingly discussed. To verify the ability of 5G networks to support V2X applications, we have built a 5G network performance road testing system aimed at real V2X applications, and conducted multiple tests on the actual 5G network, including end-to-end transmission latency and packet loss rate under different network coverage, different packet lengths, and different sending intervals. The research results show that the performance indicators of the 5G network can meet the needs of some V2I applications, which is of great reference significance for carrying out research and deployment of V2X applications based on 5G.

articleTitle: Automatic Time-Domain Gating Algorithm in FreeSpace Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: An automatic time-domain gating algorithm in freespace measurement system is proposed. Using a Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) technique, the temporal positions of the reflector plates on both sides of the sample are automatically detected. The start and end time points of the time-domain gate function are determined based on these positions. The proposed algorithm is subsequently implemented by applying the standard time-domain gating technique. The algorithm is validated using an in-house free-space measurement system. The proposed algorithm can be applied in measuring polarizer performance and dielectric constants.

articleTitle: Intelligent-Controllable Antenna Structure Based on AFSS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an intelligent controllable antenna structure based on Active Frequency Selective Surface (AFSS) is proposed by controlling PIN diodes on an off. The AFSS layer is loaded with eight pin diodes. When diodes are turned off, the FSS in the operating bandwidth shows the performance of broadband wave transmission, and the antenna radiates normally. When diodes are turned on, the AFSS becomes a metal reflector reflecting at the working bandwidth. The proposed structure can be used to realize the intelligent control of antenna radiation and improve its stealth performance.

articleTitle: A D-Band Linear Power Amplifier with Adaptive Feedback Linearizer in 40nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a two-way three-stage Dband linear power amplifier (PA) based on 40nm CMOS technology with a center frequency of 140 GHz. The PA employs an Adaptive Feedback Linearizer (AFL) for biasing to enhance linearity and utilizes a transformer-based current combining network to combine the power from the two ways to improve the output power (Pout). A gain-boosting unit (GBU) is employed in the first stage of the PA to enhance gain and multilayer stacked transformer (MLST) is used for matching networks to reduce insertion loss. Post simulation results at 1.2 V supply voltage and 140 GHz indicate the proposed PA provides 13.4 dBm of saturation output power (Psat) and 11.1 dBm of 1dB gain compression output power (OP1dB). This PA achieves 5.2% and 2% power added efficiency (PAE) at OP1dB and 6dB back-off. The small-signal gain is 11.1 dB, with a 3-dB bandwidth of 11.2 GHz, ranging from 133.9 GHz to 145.1 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a Radial Waveguide Omnidirectional Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an omnidirectional antenna based on a radial waveguide. To achieve the matching between waveguide and free space, a horn structure is employed. The antenna is coaxially fed, and an inverted cone is employed in the parallel plate for impedance matching. The antenna has strong omnidirectional radiation characteristics and operates in the 3.6 GHz to 4.35 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: Transparent Antenna with Circularly Polarized Reconfigurability for Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this work, a dual-band and circularly polarized wearable antenna with polarization reconfigurability and low visual intrusiveness is investigated. The proposed coupled-feed antenna, consisting of optically transparent and flexible materials, operates in 2.45-GHz and 3.5-GHz bands. Diagonal coupling and mutual coupling are simultaneously adopted to achieve circular polarizations at dual frequencies. By manipulating the fluidity of the liquid metal-based feed network, two reconfigurable states, including left-fright-handed circular polarizations, are realized. Besides, the antenna has the compact dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$48\times 48\times 5.5$</tex> mm 3 (0.39 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 0.39\times 0.04\lambda 0^{3},\lambda_{0}$</tex> at 2.45 GHz), making it a good candidate for wearable applications.

articleTitle: CNN-Genetic Algorithm Hybrid Approach for Rapid Inverse Design of Ultra-Wideband Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In recent years, metasurfaces have demonstrated immense potential in electromagnetic wave manipulation and antenna design. Traditional metasurface design methods heavily rely on complex numerical calculations and optimization algorithms, resulting in high computational costs and lengthy design cycles. This paper presents a novel inverse design approach combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Genetic Algorithm for metasurfaces. This method leverages CNN's advantages in feature extraction while utilizing genetic algorithm's global optimization capabilities to achieve rapid and precise design of metasurface units. Experimental results show that this approach can reduce design time from hours to minutes compared to traditional methods while maintaining high design accuracy.

articleTitle: Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Electro-Optic Modulators for Electromagnetic Field Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The design of TFLN electro-optic modulator is studied based on numerical model. By optimizing the waveguide thickness, waveguide width and electrode spacing, an electrooptic modulator applicable to the measurement of a wideband electromagnetic environment is obtained.

articleTitle: A High Power Supply Rejection NMOS LDO with Dual-Loop and Charge Pump
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a high power supply rejection (PSR) NMOS low dropout regulator (LDO) with dual-loop and charge pump. A dual-loop voltage follower that is capable of providing a high PSR through an inner fast loop and a NMOS as a power transistor. The charge pump raises the supply voltage to 1.5 times the supply voltage to power the error amplifier to ensure low dropout voltage. Post-simulation results indicate an output voltage of 896 mV with merely a 304 mV voltage dropout. The post-simulated PSR is −50 dB at 10kHz and the worst PSR of −18.7 dB at 1MHz over the full band. The undershoot/overshoot is 56 mV/12.8 mV. The total static power consumption is 756 μA.

articleTitle: Transmissive Metasurface for Generating Vortex Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In recent years, metasurfaces have developed rapidly as two-dimensional electromagnetic control devices, especially transmissive metasurfaces. In this paper, a transmissive metasurface is designed to realize the excitation of the vortex beam, and then the performance of the vortex beam is verified by simulation and measurement. Finally, a communication system was built on LABVIEW, and the wireless communication based on vortex beam was verified by combining it with the general software-defined radio peripheral USRP for wireless communication and measuring the bit error rate. In this paper, the amplitude of the transmission coefficient of the mtea-atom is higher than 0.75, the phase is 0~360° coverage, the purity of the vortex wave mode generated is higher than 65%, and the operation is in the C-band with a bandwidth of 100MHz.

articleTitle: A Simple Self-Decoupling Method for Co-Polarized In-Band Full Duplex Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a simple self-decoupling method and a corresponding radiation pattern improvement technology for co-polarized in-band full duplex (IBFD) antennas. The selfdecoupling method is implemented based on a widened planar rectangular dipole antenna. By exciting a superposed mode produced by the second- and third-order modes of the widened dipole, a specific superposed electric field can be constructed between two arms of the dipole. The transmitter port and receiver port can be located at a strong and a weak field region, respectively. As a result, a self-decoupling between TX and RX ports is realized without any extra decoupling structures or designs. Simulation shows that the antenna achieves a maximum in-band isolation of 31.5 dB at 3.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Balanced Bandpass Filter With Common-Mode Reflectionless and Suppression Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a substrate integrated waveguide balanced bandpass filter (BPF) with common-mode (CM) reflectionless and suppression characteristics. The presented BPF utilizes the triangular patches, meander-line resonators, and eighth-mode substrate integrated waveguide resonators to realize the bandpass filtering performance. Furthermore, CM reflectionless performance is achieved by adopting the two transmission lines and a grounded resistor. For demonstration, the proposed BPF design is verified, fabricated, and measured. The fabricated BPF's center frequency is 5.2 GHz, differential-mode insertion loss is 1.7 dB, 3-dB passband is 4.7-5.7 GHz, the CM reflectionless band is 3.5-7.2 GHz, the minimum CM suppression within the measured frequency range is 33 dB.

articleTitle: Design of a 3D-Printed Compact Coaxial Sleeve Bandpass Filter with High Harmonic Suppression Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This article proposes a miniaturized coaxial sleeve structure manufactured based on 3D printing technology for the first time. The resonant cavity consists of an inner column and a sleeve that is very close to each other. By reducing the distance between them, better harmonic suppression performance can be achieved without changing the volume. To verify these characteristics, a second-order single passband filter is designed, and the selectivity of the filter is improved by setting external coupling ports. The harmonic suppression multiple reaches 9.5 times and integrated printing is achieved by adding non-radiating slots. The 3D printing process can achieve the advantages of high precision and lightweight, ensuring good performance of the filter. Good agreements between the simulated results and the measured ones verify the feasibility of the proposed design method.

articleTitle: A Parallel Finite-Difference Time-Domain Framework on Heterogeneous Supercomputing Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a parallel framework for the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method on heterogeneous supercomputing platforms. The main content covers MPI parallelism, heterogeneous communication, and heterogeneous parallel acceleration. Compared to traditional MPI-based process parallel frameworks, this framework effectively leverages the characteristics of heterogeneous supercomputers. Numerical simulations validate the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Planar Wideband Circularly Polarized Antenna for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a simple structure millimeter wave circular polarization slot antenna. The slot antenna and the feed structure are printed on the positive and negative two planes of the same plate, which is the structure of a single layer of dielectric substrate and two layers of metal. Under the excitation of microstrip coupling feed, two orthogonal electric fields with orthogonal phase difference are excited at the edge of the rectangular slot with angle etched on the floor to realize circularly polarized radiation. To realize the circularly polarized radiation performance of the broad band millimeter wave, we broaden the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth by removing two angles to correct the floor shape and introducing an L-shaped slot with two angular symmetry. The antenna structure design, principle analysis and key parameters analysis. Simulation results show that the 3 dB AR bandwidth is 23.91-50.15 GHz and the 10 dB impedance bandwidth is 29.45-58.22 GHz, realizing a broadband circular polarization in the range of 29.45-50.15 GHz.

articleTitle: High-Speed and High-Robustness ESD Protection Circuit for Monolithic GaN Integrated Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces an Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) protection circuit designed for monolithic Gallium Nitride (GaN) integrated chips. Through meticulous circuit design, it proficiently regulates the gate input voltage of the primary protection GaN HEMT within the ESD circuit, thereby mitigating its on-resistance (Ron) notably. The implementation of a high gate voltage ensures swift activation of the discharge GaN HEMT during ESD events with a Double Self-Pumped ESD protection circuit, thereby significantly boosting its 3.4 times discharge capacity and enhancing the overall robustness of the ESD circuits. Furthermore, the design mitigates the reliability issue of the main protective device inadvertently turning on prematurely due to insufficient gate voltages during ESD events.

articleTitle: Beam Synthesis Method for Tri-Polarized Antenna Arrays Based on the Multi-Objective Differential Evolution (MPDE) Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a beam synthesis method for tri-polarized antenna arrays based on the multi-objective differential evolution (MPDE) algorithm. This algorithm is a swarm intelligence optimization method that relies on the convergence principle of individual gene differential iteration. It also optimizes the hemispherical multi-polarization coverage characteristics of tri-polarized antennas, effectively reducing the sidelobe levels and increasing array gain during wide-angle scanning while further suppressing sidelobe levels. Moreover, the algorithm demonstrates a significant improvement in convergence speed compared to traditional swarm optimization algorithms, and its differential iteration operator is easier to implement in hardware programming, making it suitable for high-speed beam scanning and tracking scenarios.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Resistive Ink Absorber for High Power Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A novel multilayer absorber structure using a 90degree rotational symmetric pattern is proposed. This microwave absorber is designed with an environmentally friendly resistive ink surface layer printed on dielectric board. Simulation results show that the frequency selective absorber (FSA) can achieve an absorption band of 3 - 9 GHz under normal incidence, with an electromagnetic energy absorption rate of over 90%. Under oblique incidence, the absorber maintains the same performance within the scanning range of ±50eover the whole C-band. The proposed structure employs separated dielectric boards with air spacing between them, leading to a highly practical and mature processing technique. The overall thickness is controlled to be 0.176 λ at the minimum operating frequency, making it a lowprofile design. The maximum field enhancement factor (MFEF) of the proposed structure is also calculated and displayed, which verify its application under high power microwave scenarios.

articleTitle: Generative Network-Enabled Metasurface Design for Improved Electromagnetic Transmission in Vehicle Low-E Glass
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Low-Emissivity (Low-E) glass in modern vehicles, while essential for energy efficiency, impedes electromagnetic transmission crucial for advanced communication systems. This paper presents a novel generative approach for the on-demand inverse design of meta-atoms to enhance signal transmission through automotive Low-E glass. We propose a diffusion-based framework utilizing a modified U-Net architecture with attention mechanisms and conditional information integration. Our method efficiently generates meta-atom designs meeting specific S-parameter requirements, significantly outperforming traditional optimization methods in both accuracy and speed. Experimental results demonstrate the model's capability to produce diverse, free-form metasurface unit cells, achieving a Mean Absolute Error of 0.029 on the test dataset. This approach shows promising potential for rapidly designing metasurfaces that enhance electromagnetic transmission in Low-E glass, addressing a critical challenge in automotive communication and sensor technologies.

articleTitle: A Kind of Beam-Scanning Antenna With Amplitude and Phase Control Based on SIW
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In recent years, the leaky wave antenna belongs to a kind of beam scanning antenna, which has good beam scanning ability and has been fully developed. However, it is difficult to realize fixed-frequency beam scanning in most leaky antennas, and few structures can control the amplitude and phase of electromagnetic wave simultaneously, which reduces the gain of leaky antennas and raises the sidelobe level. In this paper, a novel metasurface structure is designed and combined with SIW to achieve simultaneous amplitude and phase control, and the radiation efficiency of the unit reaches 30% when working between 7.3-7.7GHz, and the S11 is below -14dB. Finally, the genetic algorithm (GA) was selected as the control algorithm of the array factor to optimize the array and carry out simulation verification. The array has more than ±45° beam scanning capability over the operating bandwidth, with stable Y-polarization gain and sidelobe average is less than -10 dB.

articleTitle: A Cold Start Circuit with Dynamic Body Biasing for Boost Converter in RF Energy Harvesting System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a dynamic body biasing (DBB) technique is proposed and applied to a unit stage of the five-stage Dickson charge pump, which is crucial to the cold start circuit of RF energy harvesting system. Dynamic body-biasing is a wellstudied approach for MOS transistors to tune their threshold voltages, resulting in utilizing the body effect positively to improve the performance of low voltage integrated circuits. This circuit is implemented by using 65nm CMOS process. The simulated results demonstrate that this technique can provide higher current transfer via NMOS switches and improve the load capacity of the charge pump without significant power consumption. The integrated cold start circuit can operate normally with minimum input voltage of 100mV and nanowatt scale available power, and show a maximum efficiency of 60.4% at input voltage of 300mV.

articleTitle: Three-Level Chirp-Rate Shift Keying Modulation for Rotating-Magnet Based Mechanical Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper investigates a three-level Chirp-Rate Shift Keying (CSK) modulation for Rotating-magnet Based Mechanical Antenna (RMBMA), which aims to further reduce the system power consumption of the existing techniques. The reduction of system power consumption is realized by introducing “0” code without mechanical energy increment. However, the non-orthogonality of the “0” code waveform with respect to the waveforms of the “1” and “-1” codes adversely affects the system's reception performance. Wireless communication experiments were conducted with varying ratios of the “0” code, and the results indicate that a “0” code ratio of 20% optimally balances integrated system reception performance and power consumption.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Non-Classic Filter Topologies Based on Orthogonal Matrix Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this article, a semi-analytical synthesis method for filters with non-classic topologies is proposed based on orthogonal matrix decomposition. The orthogonal transform matrix of filter topology reconfiguration is decomposed into a product of rotation matrices with different pivots via the analytical Gaussian elimination method. Hence, the path of rotation transform can be obtained from these derived pivots. Once the rotation path is available, the corresponding rotation angles can be easily solved by optimization. Aided with the rotation path already figured out, the synthesis efficiency can be significantly improved. More importantly, once the topology is determined, the rotation path is not affected by the position of transmission zeros and return loss. Therefore, the obtained rotation path can be applied to accelerate the synthesis of the same class of non-classic topologies. Finally, a sixth-order filter with the extended box topology is given as an example to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: EMC and Multipath Interference Analysis in Low-Voltage Power Line Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) presents a significant challenge in power line communication (PLC) research. Power lines, originally designed for electricity distribution rather than data transmission, operate in a complex and dynamic electromagnetic environment, resulting in random noise that undermines transmission stability and reliability. This paper focuses on the modeling and mitigation of such noise. Traditional approaches, which rely on exponentially decaying sinusoidal signal models, fail to account for modern issues introduced by contemporary appliances. These include asynchronous noise from switching power supplies, synchronous noise from rectifiers, and multi-path interference caused by time-varying impedance. Here, we develop and simulate a real-world EMC model, offering new insights into these emerging challenges.

articleTitle: Communication Relationship Discovery Based on Spectrum Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of communication technology, accurately and efficiently discovering the communication relationships between communication emitters in large-scale, unevenly distributed data sets has become an important direction of current research. To address this issue, this paper proposes an adaptive clustering method called Balanced Iterative Re-ducing and Clustering Using Hierarchies- Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (BIRCH-DBSCAN) communication relationship discovery algorithm. First, the BIRCH algorithm is used to compress the large-scale spectrum data set with uneven density distribution. Next, the compressed data set is constructed into an M-nearest neighbor directed graph, and the clustering parameters for the DBSCAN algorithm are adaptively determined using the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) algorithm. Subsequently, by combining breadth-first search with matrix algebra operations, the strongly connected components in the directed graph are searched to identify the core set of classes. Finally, by matching the clustering sets, the communication relationships between transmitters are identified. Simulation results show that, compared to existing algorithms, the proposed method demonstrates superior performance in both discovery accuracy and time efficiency.

articleTitle: Active Corner Reflector Based on Electrically Tunable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Traditional corner reflectors are composed of three mutually perpendicular metal plates and represent a type of passive scatterer with fixed scattering characteristics. Herein, the authors proposed a novel electrically controlled angular reflector based on an amplitude-adjustable metasurface. Simulation results demonstrate that the active metasurface, by adjusting its electromagnetic response state through PIN diodes, achieves a dynamic adjustment of 30 dB in return loss magnitude at a frequency of 9.2 GHz. Furthermore, by integrating an amplitudeadjustable metasurface onto one surface of a traditional corner reflector, the switching between absorption and reflection states can be flexibly controlled through the powering on and off. This work significantly expands the application scenarios and scope of corner reflectors.

articleTitle: Super Low Frequency Transmitting System Based on Mechanical Antenna with Horizontal Rotating Magnet Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a horizontal rotating magnet based on mechanical antenna array method in super low frequencies to improve the radiation magnetic field strength. The array model is first discussed. Moreover, the prototype is developed. The proposed array can produce a 2.75nT magnetic field signal at the distance of 50m in the air, the corresponding effective value is achievable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$852.39\text{pT}/\sqrt{}\text{Hz}$</tex>. Finally, compared with single horizontal rotating magnetic source, the experiments verify that the o radiation magnetic field strength can be improved by 83%. This method can be used to extend the communication distance of mechanical antenna.

articleTitle: Broadband Polyomino-Shaped Antenna Elements and Array Based on Substrate Integrated Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a series of broadband polyomino-shaped high-order-mode back-cavity slot antenna (PS-HOM- BSA) elements based on substrate integrated cavity (SIC) are proposed for fifth-generation (5G) applications. Irregular SIC is used for the first time to design high-order-mode back-cavity slot antenna (HOM-BSA). The simulated results show that the -10 dB impedance bandwidth of all elements can fully cover 5G communication bands n257, n258 and n261 (19.54%, 24.25-29.5 GHz). A periodic array and an aperiodic array with the same number of feeding ports and radiation slots based on some of these elements are also given. The simulated results show that the aperiodic array is beneficial for designing low sidelobe antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Modeling of GaN HEMTs Based on BP Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Gallium nitride (GaN) high electron-mobility tran-sistors (HEMTs) serve as an important link in Radio Frequency (RF) circuits, so its accurate modeling becomes crucial. Tra-ditional modeling is based on physical formula, which is not only inconvenient to calculate but also needs to consider a large number of influencing factors. With the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), this paper proposes a new modeling method for GaN HEMTs based on Back Propagation (BP) neural networks. The method eliminates the complex physical computation steps and trains the neural network only by using actual input and output data to obtain the model. Compared with the traditional modeling, the method eliminates the com-plex physical formula calculation step, which is not only simple but also more accurate. The experimental results show that the model has excellent performance on both large-signal and small-signal models of GaN HEMTs.

articleTitle: Amorphous Silicon for Parasitic Surface Conduction Effect Elimination of SAW Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This work presents a surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator based on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{LiTaO}_{3}/\text{SiO}_{2}/\text{amorphous}$</tex> silicon <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\alpha$</tex>–Si)/crystalline silicon (c-Si) multilayer substrate. Oxide-passivated high resistivity (HR) wafers lead to experiencing parasitic surface conduction (PSC) caused by fixed charges in the oxide. A thin layer of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>–-Si eliminates the PSC effect to reduce substrate loss. The substrate loss is extracted by coplanar waveguide structure in HFSS. The fabricated resonator shows a high Bode-Q of 2040 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k^{2}{}_{\text{eff}}$</tex> of 11.6%. The performance has shown the strong potential of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{LiTaO}_{3}/\text{SiO}_{2}/\alpha-\text{Si}/\text{Si}$</tex> multilayer substrate for the front-end applications in 5G.

articleTitle: A V-Band Power Amplifier with 28.2% PAE and 21.4 dBm Output Power in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This work presents a CMOS broadband millimeter-wave power amplifier (PA) based on 65-nm CMOS process. The PA includes two stages of common-source (CS) driver amplifiers along with one cascode stage. The PA utilizes the gain compensation near the compression point in the second-stage driver and the power stage to improve linearity while maintaining gain. Simulation results show that the proposed PA achieves a peak gain (S21) of 22.3 dB with a 3-dB bandwidth ranging from 52.5 to 81.5 GHz. The PA achieves 28.2% peak power added efficiency (peak PAE), 21.4 dBm saturated output power (Psat), and 20.3 dBm output 1-dB compression point (OP1dB) with 26.2% power added efficiency (PAE).

articleTitle: Adaptive Parallel DCSK with Code Index Modulation for Implantable Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Intra-body communication is limited by the complex biological organization of the human body, and the signal is subject to severe attenuation and multipath interference during propagation. In this paper, an adaptive parallel transmission with code-indexed modulation and differential chaotic shift keying (A-PT-CIM-DCSK) technique is proposed for implantable sensor networks. The number of parallel transmission channels is adaptively adjusted through least squares for channel estimation to achieve optimal transmission, enhancing the robustness of the system while maintaining a high data rate. The computational complexity is reduced by the cyclic shift of chaotic sequences. The theoretical bit error rate (BER) formula of A-PT-CIM-DCSK over the generalized Nakagami channel is derived, and its performance is verified by Monte Carlo simulations. The simulation results show that compared with the conventional CIM-DCSK system, the proposed scheme can achieve higher data rates while maintaining a lower BER over intra-body fading channels.

articleTitle: AII-Textile Antenna With On-/ Off-Body Reconfigurability in Single Band for Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A flexible reconfigurable antenna operating in the 2.45-GHz ISM band with on- and off-body modes is proposed for wearable devices. Omnidirectional and unidirectional radiations are constructed using the fundamental TMoo and TM modes in the rectangular patch. The resonance of the unidirectional mode is introduced to the operating band by four set slots, and circular polarization of the unidirectional radiation is achieved by cutting corners diagonally across the patch. The radiation modes are controlled by four PIN diodes. The simulated -10-dB impedance bandwidths of on- and off-body modes are 3.47% (2.40-2.485 GHz) and 3.47% (2.40-2.485 GHz), respectively. The 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth in unidirectional radiation is 0.6% (2.439-2.454 GHz) when the antenna is attached to a multilayer human tissue model.

articleTitle: Wideband Differential-Fed Filtering Antenna Based on LTCC for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband filtering antenna based on Low Temperature Co-Fired Ceramic (LTCC) technology for 5G millimeter-wave applications. The design features a radiation patch, a driven patch and two sets of planar inverted-F antennas (PIFAs). The proposed antenna is fed by a set of differential microstrip lines through aperture coupling. Besides, two pairs of PIFA antennas generate two lower-band radiation zeros, while a set of U-shape slots etched into the ground plane creates an additional upper-band radiation zero. These structures enhance the filtering function while expanding the operational bandwidth to 24.25-29.5 GHz, efficiently covering the 5G n257/n258/n261 frequency bands. The antenna's dimensions are compact, measuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.56\lambda_{c}\times 0.56\lambda_{c}\times 0.1\lambda_{c}$</tex> at 28 GHz. The simulation results verify that the impedance bandwidth is 39.1% (23.21-34.5 GHz) and the antenna achieves over 13 dB of gain suppression in the out-of-band frequencies, effectively suppressing unwanted signal gain. The proposed antenna features compact, wideband and filtering characteristics, which is attractive for 5G millimeter-wave mobile communications.

articleTitle: MIMO Capacity Analysis of Wearable Antennas in FR3 Lower Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper analyzes the channel capacity of wearable antennas in the FR3 lower band (7 GHz). Based on the dynamic motion of human arm swinging, the channel capacities of four different wearable MIMO arrays arrangements are analyzed using a Monte Carlo simulation algorithm. The difference caused by the utilized channel model, Clarke's model and the Cluster model, was compared. The average channel capacity obtained under the Clarke model maintains at 28.5 bits/s/Hz. On the other hand, when using the Cluster model, the wide range fluctuation of MIMO capacity between 18.5 bitslslHz and 32.6 bitslslHz is observed. This fact reveals that the MIMO capacity of a wearable antenna under the Cluster model is more dependent on the practical use scenarios compared to that of the Clarke's model.

articleTitle: A Self-Reconfigurable Impedance Matching Network for a Wideband Radio Frequency Energy Harvester in 65nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband radio frequency energy harvester with the use of a novel, digitally controlled impedance matching network (IMN) operating in the 850 MHz to 950 MHz frequency band. The proposed design utilizes a Lumped (Shunt) Reactance Cancellation L-Type impedance matching network (IMN). With this design, manipulation of impedance values becomes possible making impedance matching between complex sources and load sources at different frequencies. The circuit was implemented in 65nm CMOS technology. The system achieved a peak PCE of 78.26% at −14 dBm input power and a load of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{100\mathrm{k}}\Omega$</tex>. The design exhibited a DR of 16.31 dB and a sensitivity at 1V of −14 dBm at 900 MHz. The design offers a return loss of −10 dB across the frequency range with a peak value of −41.92 dB. The integration of the control circuit is influenced by input power levels. The system effectively operates from −17 dBm to higher power levels, with optimal matching for 850 MHz to 950 MHz at −10 dBm input power.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Parallel DGTD Calculation Method Based on DSP Clusters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper is based on a domestic supercomputer to evaluate the performance of the parallel discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method. In conjunction with the MT3000 digital signal processor (DSP) platform, this paper introduces parallel schemes at both coarse-grained process level and fine-grained thread level, and proposes a method for accelerating the DGTD matrix solution on a CPU-DSP heterogeneous platform. The test results indicate that when expanded from 8 processes to 160 processes, the method maintains a parallel efficiency of 50.6% while ensuring accuracy.

articleTitle: Timing Analysis of AVB Traffic in 5G-TSN Networks Using Network Calculus
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The proposal of Ultra-Reliable and Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) has promoted the new research trend of integration of 5G and TSN. There are currently few studies on the probabilistic E2E delay of the integrated 5G-TSN network. Therefore, in this paper, we deduce the probabilistic E2E delay bound of Audio-Video-Bridging (AVB) traffic in the integrated 5G-TSN network, considering the influence of DRR scheduling strategy, AVB traffic characteristics, and Rayleigh's fading channel fading. Our findings indicate that a more stringent upper bound on latency is achieved. In order to improve E2E delay, the number of resource blocks (RBs) allocated should be correctly distributed in accordance with a match requirement of delay upper bound and dependability.

articleTitle: Wireless Federated Learning with Retransmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables distributed devices to collaboratively train a shared machine learning (ML) model while protecting their data privacy. However, the limited radio resources of mobile devices and unreliable channels pose per-formance bottlenecks for deploying FL over wireless networks. In this paper, we propose a novel federated learning framework with frequency-diverse retransmission to address these issues. First, we analyze the impact of unreliable transmission on the convergence rate. Next, we formulate an optimal resource block (RB) allocation problem to minimize the model convergence error subject to the energy budget. To solve this problem, we transform it into a multiple-choice knapsack problem and use dynamic programming to solve it. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed scheme compared to the benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: Aperture-Shared Base-Station Antenna Array Design Based on EM Transparency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A dual-polarized antenna designed for electromagnetic (EM) transparency is introduced as a low-band (LB) antenna within an aperture-shared antenna system ensuring the radiation pattern of high-band (HB) antenna remains intact. The EM transparency is accomplished by incorporating two types of cross-slots into the radiator of LB antenna. These two types of cross-slots are overlapped together to form a composite resonant slot. Since the bandpass response in HB, the composite resonant slots contribute to counter the radiation of HB induced currents on the LB antenna, resulting in minimal impact on the radiation patterns of the HB antenna. For demonstration, a prototype dual-band antenna array has been constructed, covering the LB of 1.7-2.56GHz (VSWR<1.5) and the HB of 3.3-3.8GHz (VSWR<1.5), is fabricated. The simulation results confirm effectiveness of the array in preserving the radiation performance of the HB antenna.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Folded Reflectarray Antenna with ME Dipole Feed at K-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this work, a circularly polarized folded reflectarray antenna (CPFRA) with a linearly polarized feed was proposed for K-band satellite communication uplinks. The main reflector consists of double quasi-I-beam elements achieving 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∘</sup> phase shifts and linear polarization rotation. A polarization-selective surface is used as the sub-reflector, and its linear polarization reflection efficiency and circular polarization conversion are analyzed. Moreover, a magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna is designed as the feed, offering wide bandwidth, low cross-polarization, and ease of integration with the main reflector. The proposed CPFRA features a low profile, compact structure, and a low axial ratio. Simulation results demonstrate that the antenna achieves a 1-dB gain bandwidth of 19.16% (17.7-21.45 GHz), a 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 8.46% (19.24-20.94 GHz), and a maximum gain of 22.5 dBi at 20 GHz.

articleTitle: Advancing the Optimization of Cross-Dipole Antennas Through Pixelated Design Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A novel cross dipole antenna, utilizing pixelation for design, is proposed. The unique feature of this antenna in that the use of pixels to shape the radiator through an Internal Multi-port Method (IMPM), ensuring impedance matching and bandwidth performance. This approach overcomes manual design limitations and yields performance metrics comparable to conventional methods while enhancing simulation design efficiency. By using this method, the impedance bandwidth achieved at port 1 of the antenna amounts to 50.5% (∣S11∣ < 10 dB within 1.66–2.78 GHz), the impedance bandwidth at port 2 is 51.4% (∣S22∣<10dB within 1.66-2.81GHz), and the isolation between the two ports can reach 25 dB within the frequency band.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Transmitarray Antenna with High Selective Gain Filtering Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel low-profile transmitarray antenna with high selective gain filtering performance is proposed. The proposed transmitarray unit cell is comprised of a magneto-electric (ME) dipole and a split-ring resonator. The ME dipole provides radiation zero at low frequency, and the splitring resonator provides radiation zero at high frequency. The transmission phase of 0° and 180° can be realized by rotating the bottom feed structure in the radiation band. The thickness of the transmitarray unit cell is 3.1mm (0.106λ). Based on the unit cell, a circular transmitarray antenna with a center frequency of 10.3GHz and a diameter of 221.2mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(7.6\lambda)$</tex> is designed. The simulation result shows that the transmitarray achieves a 3dB gain bandwidth of 12.3%, the highest gain is 20.07dBi, the suppression level at low and high frequencies are 27.4dB and 17.7dB, respectively. And the calculated selectivity is 0.86. A high selectivity and low profile is implemented.

articleTitle: A DC-50 GHz 6-bit Digital-Step Attenuator with 31.5 dB Tuning Range in 28-nm Bulk CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This letter presents a DC-50 GHz 6-bit digital-step attenuator (DSA). By using capacitive compensation technology and phase compensation structure, the amplitude error and phase variation is reduced. The attenuator is fabricated using TSMC 28-nm bulk CMOS process, with a core area of 0.063 mm2, The measured insertion loss of the attenuator at working frequency of DC to 50 GHz is 2.37 - 11 dB. The total attenuation range is 31.5 dB with a step of 0.5 dB. Within the 31.5 dB tuning range, the attenuator has a maximum phase variation of 12° and an RMS phase variation of 6.4°, with a maximum amplitude error of 1.2 dB.

articleTitle: Study on the Mechanism of High Power Microwave Radiation Effect of GaN LNA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a high-power microwave resonant cavity is designed and used to build a high-power microwave radiation experimental system, and the high-power microwave radiation interference effect of GaN low-noise amplifier is studied. Unlike lots of previous papers whose research focuses on the high-power microwave injection damage effects of RF front-end devices, this paper proposes a simple high-power microwave radiation testing system, which can generate a high-power microwave radiation field of 100kV/m under continuous wave and pulse working conditions. The gain of GaN LNA decreases with the increase of high-power microwave radiation field strength, mainly due to the vertical high-power microwave radiation equal to the injection power to the input port of LNA, which causes saturation of the LNA, and reduces its linearity and amplification ability for weak signals. This experimental system greatly reduces the high cost, difficulty, and safety requirements of traditional high-power microwave effect systems. It has certain practical value for conducting high-power microwave radiation experiments on digital circuits such as MCU and FPGA, as well as analog circuit components such as limiters and amplifiers.

articleTitle: A High-Precision Target Detection Algorithm Based on a Small Amount of Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Millimeter-wave body scanners have emerged as a key technology in modern security inspection systems. However, the limited availability of datasets for training models in this field makes it challenging to achieve high-precision detection. In this paper, we propose an optimized approach for detecting dangerous objects using a limited dataset. By leveraging YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 models, the proposed method can achieve an accuracy of 75.1% even with a limited dataset, ensuring practical applicability for real-world security scenarios. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in maintaining high detection performance despite data limitations.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Dual-Channel Dielectric Filter Based on Ceramic Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a low-cost monolithic dual-channel filter based on ceramic additive manufacturing technology is proposed. Utilizing ceramic 3D printing, the resonators (DRs) and the cavity are integrated into a single piece, leading to substantial reductions in manufacturing costs and the elimination of alignment problems. To construct dual channels in the same DR, a dual-mode DR is obtained by constructing a hybrid electromagnetic (EM) boundary by partially connecting the DR with the ceramic cavity. Moreover, a cross-shaped ceramic structure is used as coupling windows. For validation, a monolithic dual-channel filter is fabricated and measured. The measured results show good filtering response and high inter-channel isolation.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Folded Monopole Antenna with Low Profile for Partial Discharge Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband folded monopole antenna with vertical polarization is proposed for partial discharge detection. The antenna incorporates a top loading and four grounded pins for impedance matching and maintaining a low profile. The radiator size of the antenna is 0.3λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.3λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> X 0.107λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the wavelength corresponding to the lowest frequency). The measured results show that the proposed antenna has an ultra-wide impedance bandwidth of 157.7% for a reflection coefficient ≤ -10 dB, ranging from 0.36 GHz to 3.05 GHz, meeting the frequency-band requirement for partial discharge detection. The antenna achieves a realized gain ranging from 0.4 to 7.2 dBi. It also exhibits quasi-omnidirectional far-field radiation patterns.

articleTitle: On-Chip Topological Waveguides and Cavities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Topological photonics offers a powerful platform for next-generation nanophotonic chips, capitalizing on their remarkable resilience to disorder and defects. In this paper, we'll present a series of on-chip topological devices, including topological photonic cavity supporting lateral beam shifts, topological cavity confined at the topological corner states, terahertz (THz) valley-spin-valley converter, and THz taper-free topological waveguide.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Leadless Packaged SPDT PIN Switch
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: According to our GaAs PIN diode process, we have successfully implemented a highly integrated, broadband, leadless PIN switch. In the 10GHz∼18GHz frequency band, the port stand wave is lower than 1.3, the insertion loss is less than 1.5dB, the isolation is greater than 25dB. The package size is limited to 4.0mm*4.0mm*1.2mm. The development of leadless package SPDT PIN switch will improve the technique of higher integration, lower system cost and smaller array area.

articleTitle: Time Modulated mm-Wave Transceiver Chips With Enhanced Backoff Efficiency (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of a time-modulated transmitter array that improves efficiency in mmWave transmitters by integrating direct digital amplitude and phase beamforming. Traditional systems face challenges with low backoff efficiency and complex beamforming at high frequencies. The time modulated system addresses these by using time modulation to control phase shifting and backoff, providing enhanced power efficiency and harmonic suppression. The key innovation is introducing a new concept of using time as an additional degree of freedom, with time-modulated digital switching to precisely control phase and improve efficiency across a wide range of backoff levels. This method simplifies hardware by eliminating the need for bulky phase shifters, while enabling precise beamforming and frequency agility, making the system scalable for large phased arrays.

articleTitle: Compact Ultra-Wideband Planar Antenna with Rectangular ring for Stable Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This work presents a compact planar antenna producing stable gain and radiation pattern in an ultrawide operating bandwidth. By adding a rectangular ring to the conical patch antenna, the bandwidth of the antenna is extended effectively while the lowest resonant frequency is reduced. Simulated results show that the proposed antenna has a bandwidth of 93% (0.8 GHz - 2.2 GHz). Stable radiation patterns are generated within the bandwidth. The peak gain of the antenna varies between 1.8 dBi and 2.5 dBi. This design provides a new perspective and solution for the advancement of compact ultra-wideband antenna design.

articleTitle: An Attention Mechanism Spatio-Temporal Graph Framework for Misbehavior Detection in IoV
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing interest in applying Deep Learning (DL) techniques for Misbehavior Detection in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). Despite this, network anomalies caused by various attack types continue to pose significant challenges, such as incomplete misbehavior detection, inefficient multi-model detection, and insufficient accuracy. To address these issues, this paper introduces a novel detection framework, specifically designed for the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), which is called Attention Mechanism Spatio-Temporal Graph Framework (ATG). In contrast to traditional DL models, the framework is a multi-classification model that integrates Graph Neural Network (GNN), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Spatial Attention Mechanism. The proposed scheme enhances feature engineering through the Attention Mechanism, utilizes a node aggregation algorithm within the GNN, and achieves global detection via the GRU. Experimental results demonstrate the model's performance in different environments using the dataset generated in Veins, and provide a comparison with baseline methods. Under typical conditions, the model achieves an accuracy of 94.6%, a precision of 88.8%, a recall of 90.9%, and an F1-Score of 89.1%. ATG shows a precision improvement of 1-10% and a recall improvement of 1-16% compared to other schemes, demonstrating enhanced security and reliability.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network-Assisted Anti-Resonance Hollow Core Fiber Confinement Loss Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: One of the critical performance metrics of anti-resonant fibers(ARFs) is the confinement loss of the fundamental mode, and achieving a lower confinement loss is one of the primary objectives in current design endeavors. Traditionally, the process of obtaining the confinement loss of designed fibers through simulation software like COMSOL is excessively time-intensive. To expedite the modeling process of anti-resonant fibers, this paper explores how to leverage a well-trained artificial neural network for rapid simulation of anti-resonant fibers while achieving high-precision output predictions. In the proposed method, an artificial neural network model is established to effectively map the feature space to the target optical characteristics. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated using a specific structure of anti-resonant fiber as an example.

articleTitle: Generation of Linearly Polarized Airy Beam
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a method for generating Airy beams in the microwave band by employing 1-bit phase control via metasurfaces. The study also includes theoretical and simulation-based validations of the Airy beam's properties, curvature control, and self-focusing capabilities, demonstrating its potential applications in the Internet of Things (IoT) and optical communications.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Multi-Layer Common-Mode Filter Based on Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative multi-layer millimeter-wave broadband common-mode filter (CMF). The equivalent circuit of defected ground structure (DGS) expressed by transmission line model is provided and analyzed. The simulated results agree well with the full-wave simulation results. To avoid electromagnetic (EM) shielding effects, multi-layer circuit design is given to make it applicable for practical manufacture. For the proposed common mode filter, the corresponding 10.9-GHz common-mode (CM) stopband bandwidth covers 21.5-32.4 GHz. Moreover, the 3-dB differential mode (DM) cutoff frequency can reach up to 38.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband High-Efficiency Rectifier Based on Coupled Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-wideband rectifier based on coupled transmission line, which achieves high-efficient rectification in a compact and simple configuration. Through theoretical analysis and simulation validation, the proposed rectifier exhibits favorable rectifying performance, achieving an ultra-wide bandwidth of 128.1% ranging from 1.86 GHz to 8.49 GHz with an input power of 15 dBm. In addition, the efficiency of the proposed rectifier exceeds 50% within the whole bandwidth and the peak efficiency reaches 68.4%. The simulated results suggest that the proposed rectifier is promising for radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting.

articleTitle: Modeling Method for Curved Surface of Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a modeling method for Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) units on curved surfaces. By fine-tuning the shape of FSS units on the unfolded surface, precise arrangement on surface is achieved, avoid residual subarraying. This design not only enables a more complete layout of the array in the overall structure but also demonstrates excellent electromagnetic performance. It addresses limitations in traditional design methods for arranging on curved surfaces and improves the overall stealth performance.

articleTitle: Precise Impedance Matching for Class- E Driven MHz WPT System Based on Mobius Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In MHz wireless power transfer (WPT) systems, load conditions often fluctuate due to coil misalignment, impedance changes, or compensation errors. However, the Class-E power amplifier (PA), which commonly used in high-frequency wireless power transfer, is sensitive to load variations and thus lacks overall robustness. To enhance the stability of the Class-E PA, an impedance matching network (IMN) is required, but the IMN itself has limited design degrees of freedom, making it challenging to accurately pull multiple load points to designed working conditions. Addressing these challenges, this paper proposes a novel matching network design method based on Mobius transformation. The IMN designed with proposed method enables a Class-E PA to operate efficiently at different situations as changing resistive loads or compensation errors. The effectiveness of the design has been verified through simulation and experiment. The system designed with proposed method has 84%-87% DC-DC system efficiency with 40% mutual inductance variation.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Intelligent Reflecting Surface for 5G Coverage Extension With Stable Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel wideband single-layer passive intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) designed to enhance 5G network coverage and ensure stable beam steering. The proposed IRS operates across the full spectrum of 5G mmWave bands, specifically targeting the n258 and n257 bands. The design features an upper layer composed of sub-wavelength unit cells, each with a periodicity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.43\lambda$</tex> at 26 GHz and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.46\lambda$</tex> at 28 GHz. The phase compensation on the IRS aperture, consisting of 40 × 40 unit cells and measuring 200 mm × 200 mm × 1.5 mm, is engineered to improve 5G signal quality in areas prone to signal degradation, with a 5G base station positioned 10 meters away. The IRS reflects incident 5G signals from the base station at an angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta_{i}=-15^{\circ}$</tex>, directing the enhanced signal to receivers and users at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta_{r}=30^{\circ}$</tex>. Both simulation and empirical results confirm that the proposed IRS effectively covers the entire 24 to 30 GHz millimeter-wave band, can enhance 5G signal strength and extend 5G coverage in areas where direct line-of-sight to the base station is obstructed or weak, ensures consistent beam steering performance across the frequency range.

articleTitle: Fast Response and Miniaturized Phase Shifter Based on Liquid Crystal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a fast response and miniaturized phase shifter is proposed based on liquid crystals (LCs). The proposed phase shifter is implemented utilizing a slot line-based loaded line structure. The high characteristic impedance of the slot line effectively enhances the phase-shifting capability per wavelength, facilitating the miniaturized design. A cascaded ABCD matrix is employed to analyze the electromagnetic characteristics of the periodic unit, guiding the phase shifter design. In addition, a high-impedance bias network is adopted to apply DC bias. The experimental validation illustrates that the proposed phase shifter achieves a phase shift of 225° per wavelength at 14.125 GHz. The reflection coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert S_{11}$</tex> remains below -10 dB across the 13 GHz to 15 GHz, and the figure of merit (FoM) reaches 118.7°/dB at 14.125 GHz. Furthermore, the millisecond-level response time provides additional competitive advantages for high-frequency applications, particularly in potential uses for satellite communications and radar systems.

articleTitle: A 95.71% Power Efficiency DC-DC PFM Boost Converter with Recursive Voltage Supply Technique for Low-Power Energy Harvesting Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a highly efficient DC-DC Pulse Frequency Modulation (PFM) boost converter, tailored for low-power energy harvesting applications, utilizing a recursive voltage supply technique. Designed and simulated using 22nm FDSOI technology in Cadence Virtuoso, the converter demonstrates remarkable performance under varying load and input conditions. The system achieves a stable output voltage with minimal drop, even as the input voltage fluctuates between 300mV and 500mV. Efficiency measurements show up to 95.71% efficiency at lower input voltages, with consistent performance across different load currents. This work represents a significant advancement in energy-efficient electronics, addressing the growing demand for sustainable and autonomous power management solutions.

articleTitle: An Ultra-wideband Reconfigurable Transmitarray Using Tightly Coupled Dipole Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband, tightly coupled, reconfigurable transmitarray (UTRTA) with 50° beam scanning capability is proposed. The ultra-wideband performance of the array is improved by optimizing the coupling effects between adjacent elements, and a 1-bit reconfigurable phase function is achieved using a current path reversal mechanism. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16 \times 16$</tex> UTRTA is designed, demonstrating a peak gain of 19.6 dBi (10.5 GHz), and a simulated 3 dB gain bandwidth of 29.3% (12.2 to 16.4 GHz). Additionally, the array achieves a 0° to 50° beam scanning range in the E-plane with a gain reduction of no more than 1.4 dB. This proposed UTRTA features a wide transmission band and reconfigurable phase functionality, which makes it a good candidate for wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A 6–14 GHz GaN Power Amplifier With 45.3 dBm Output Power Using Real-to-Real Matching Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a high-power monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) power amplifier (PA) using 0.25 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> Gallium Nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) technology, operating in the frequency range of 6–14 GHz. A real-to-real output matching network is employed to achieve impedance matching at a fundamental level. Compared to traditional approaches, the proposed design method provides the advantage of simplicity, especially for MMIC designs. Furthermore, active compensation for gain roll-off is implemented in the input matching network and inter-stage matching network to achieve excellent small-signal gain flatness. The PA, with a chip size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.05\times 2.44\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>, exhibits an output power of 45.3 to 46.7 dBm, with a power-added efficiency ranging from 27.2% to 32.5% at a drain voltage of 28 V.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Calibration Device for 2450MHz Microwave Leakage Meter Based on Waveguide Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The waveguide method is a method provided in the IEEE Std 1309 standard for calibrating field probes and field sensors, particularly suitable for the calibration of microwave leakage meters. Compared with traditional standard field methods, its biggest advantages are low cost, small size, and the ability to generate large field strengths with only a small power input, which can meet the calibration of some large range power density points. Based on the working principle of waveguide method, the theoretical derivation of waveguide method has been improved, and a low-cost, miniaturized, and large range 2450MHz microwave leakage energy meter calibration device has been designed. Simulation and experimental results show that the calibration device can effectively meet the calibration requirements of commonly used 2450MHz microwave leakage meters.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Analysis of LDO Circuit Boards Under EFT Interference Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper tests and analyses the performance of low-dropout regulator (LDO) circuit boards under electrically fast transient (EFT) interference sources. The input and output states of the device under test are monitored by the direct power injection method to describe the operating state and performance changes of the board under different interference conditions and to analyze its response characteristics under different EFT interference intensities. Measurement results show that when EFT interference is applied to the Signal injection end, transient pulses of several tens of volts are generated at the monitoring end. As the interference intensity increases, the stability and efficiency of the LDO board do not show significant changes. It shows a strong anti-interference ability and stability performance. Finally, this paper further discusses the key factors and optimization directions in the design of LDO circuit boards, which provides a reliable reference for understanding and solving the internal failure mechanism of the chip and the performance of its components of LDO circuit boards under EFT interference.

articleTitle: Design of Low Band Transmission and High Band Absorption FSR Based on Coding Metasurface
