publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a frequency selective Rasorber (FSR) based on coding metasurface. The overall structure is a traditional 2-D FSR structure. The surface of the lossy layer is a checkerboard distributed coding structure, which is composed of several square resistance film patches of the same size. The surface and back of the FSS layer are loaded with metal patches of the same size. Through the combination of topology optimization and improved estimation of distribution algorithm (IEDA), the |S21| of the designed structure is greater than -3dB in the broadband range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\sim 5.44\text{GHz}$</tex>. In the broadband range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.30\text{GHz}\sim 18.62\text{GHz}$</tex>, the absorption rate is greater than 90%, up to 99%, with excellent high-frequency absorption performance. The research results have broad application prospects in the field of radar stealth radome.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Limitations behind Wide-band Holographic Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Focusing on the electromagnetic limitations behind wide-band holographic communications, we investigate the embedded element efficiency of infinite regular antenna arrays with non-ideal matching networks. Under practical considerations, the approximated embedded element efficiency is obtained and utilized to calculate the spectral efficiency of a wide-band holographic MIMO system. By numerical simulations, it is shown that the intensity of mutual coupling among array elements varies according to the operating frequency. Moreover, even if non-ideal matching networks are taken into account, element spacing of half wavelength is still the most economical and practical choice of modern communication systems.

articleTitle: Optically Transparent Intelligent Reflecting Surface for 5G and Future 6G Coverage Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an optically transparent intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) for 5G and future 6G network coverage enhancement using indium tin oxide (ITO) material. The proposed transparent IRS consists of a patterned ITO sheet with a surface impedance of 2.5 ohm/sq. Due to the high loss characteristics of ITO, a multilayer unit cell structure is employed to reduce dielectric losses. Simulating a single ITO-based unit cell revealed challenges in achieving a 360° phase shift with low reflection loss. Therefore, two unit cells are utilized to provide the required 360° phase compensation across the IRS aperture with less than 5 dB losses for both unit cells. An optically transparent IRS with 40x40 cells (200 mm×200 mm) is designed to reflect incoming signals from a base station 10 meters away toward a blind zone with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta_{i}=-15^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta_{r}{ = }$</tex> -37°. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed optically transparent IRS effectively covers the entire 5G millimeter-wave band from 24–30 GHz, maintaining stable beamforming performance throughout the frequency range.

articleTitle: Study on Time-domain Characteristics of Waveguide Plasma Limiter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: To effectively avoid damage to sensitive microwave devices caused by high-power microwaves, this paper selects argon gas as the filling gas and proposes a waveguide plasma limiter model. This model can seal low-gas-pressure inert gases and increase local field strength. Under high power, it can respond quickly and has a high degree of isolation, but when the high power ends, it can recover to an unlimited state. Based on the finite element method, a plasma fluid model is used for numerical simulation to obtain the time-domain evolution characteristics of electron density, electric field, etc. The numerical results indicate that at the beginning, the gas around the discharge electrode in the limiter is strongly ionized and forms a short road surface, reflecting microwave pulses, and the electron concentration at the subsequent electrode decreases; As time goes on, due to the formation of a short road surface at the front electrode, the electric field at the resonant window gradually reaches its maximum, and the electron density at the resonant window also increases rapidly. The high-density plasma region gradually moves towards the incident end, ultimately achieving stability. Within a certain electron density range, the initial electron density does not affect whether a plasma is formed, but only the length of time it takes to form a plasma. The research in this paper can provide a theoretical basis for the design and optimization of microwave plasma limiters.

articleTitle: Research on Forward Design Method for Airport Pavements Based on BIM Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: To address the challenges of forward design in airport design practices, including improving design consistency, quality, and reducing time cost when converting BIM models, this paper proposed a method based on BIM technology. Leveraging the BIMBase platform's potential ability to manage terrain and large-scale models, and aligning with the airport pavement design workflow, we developed a business logic-based forward design methodology. Using the C++ API interface provided in the SDK, we created the “Airport Pavement Design System”. Practical proj ects implementations demonstrate that the method and system align well with design practices and enable simultaneously output of both 2D design and 3D models in airport pavement engineering. This approach has significant potential for application in future projects.

articleTitle: A High Energy Efficiency Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Electromagnetic Scattering Analysis of Electrically Extra Large Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In the fields of weapon platform stealth design and radar target recognition, there is an urgent need for precise electromagnetic scattering analysis of complex, largescale objects (» 1000 wavelengths). Although existing algorithms strive to address these problems, they often require enormous computational resources (Over 10000 CPU cores and 100 TB of memory), with computation times extending into the hundreds of hours. These traditional methods are characterized by low energy efficiency and cannot guarantee computational accuracy. To tackle these challenges, this article presents an innovative Discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method. By integrating prior electromagnetic phase information into the numerical framework, this method dramatically reduces computational complexity and enhances energy efficiency. The performance of this solver is demonstrated through an aircraft carrier scattering model that spans more than 2400 wavelengths, highlighting its robustness and superior energy efficiency.

articleTitle: A Novel Improved Symmetric Coprime MIMO Array for DOA Estimation of Coherent Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Compared to the traditional passive detection co-prime array, coprime MIMO array has the advantage of detecting coherent signals. Compared to other coprime MIMO arrays, the symmetric coprime MIMO array (SCMA) has more subarrays, making it more flexible. However, the SCMA array contains a significant amount of redundancy. In this paper, a new improved SCMA structure is proposed, which not only reduces the redundancy of the SCMA but also utilizes the information from the redundant sensors to obtain more degrees of freedom (DoFs) and a larger virtual aperture, thereby improving the estimation accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: A 37-40 GHz Low-Power Low Noise Amplifier in 65-nm RF CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a low noise amplifier (LNA) with a bandwidth of 37–40 GHz., referred to as n260 in the FR2-band for 5G communication., implemented using 65-nm CMOS technology. Instead of using traditional LC matching networks., transformers are used for impedance matching. The LNA adopts a two-stage cascade configuration., which uses a common-source (CS) structure for the first stage and a common-source common-gate (Cascode) structure for the second stage. By limiting the operating current of the transistors., the power consumption of the entire circuit is only 7.5 mW with 1.2-V supply voltage. The proposed LNA achieves a peak gain of 16 dB with gain flatness of less than 1 dB in the Ka-band. The post-simulated noise figure (NF) is 4.9-5.2 dB from 37.5 to 39.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A Load-Independent Choke-Less Class-E Power Amplifier for 6.78-MHz Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Class E power amplifier (PA) is a single-switch inverter widely used in high-frequency applications. In the Class E PA topology, a large enough choke inductor is required to maintain a constant input current. This bulky choke inductor reduces the PA's energy density and introduces extra losses. To eliminate the influence of this choke inductor and make the system more compact, a load-independent choke-less power amplifier topology for wireless power transfer (WPT) application is proposed. The waveform characteristics are derived analytically. A load-independent design method is introduced to guarantee the high efficiency of the inverter under any loading condition. A WPT system is implemented to verify the load-independent design concept.

articleTitle: A Study of Mesh Quality Indicators for Computational Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a study of mesh quality indicators for computational electromagnetics (CEM) methods. Taking the electric field integral equation (EFIE) as example, five geometric-based mesh quality indicators are discussed. Based on the artificial neural networks, the conditional numbers of the impedance matrix can be linked to those indicators, where it could be thus predicted as output. More than 5000 meshing data are trained, and numerical examples show that the conditional number could be accurately fitted and employed to predicate the mesh quality. This study is useful for the mesh quality evaluation and optimization of the pre-processing in EM computational methods.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Polarized Linear Array for 5G mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A dual-polarized wideband millimeter-wave(mm-wave) phased linear array has been designed. The two polarization directions of the antenna are formed by planar ultrawideband modular antenna array (PUMA) and Magnetoelectric (ME) dipole, Overcoming the problem of insufficient coupling in one polarization direction of a 1-D dual polarized tightly coupled linear array. Simulation results indicate that the infinite array can cover a bandwidth of 24.25 to 40 GHz, containing the 5G NR frequency bands n257, n258, n260, and n261. It can achieve 30° scanning for pol-x and pol-y. By combining the wideband performance of these two types of antennas, a 1 ×8 finite linear array can simultaneously meet the requirements for bandwidth and scanning angle.

articleTitle: Power Allocation for FAS-assisted Downlink Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Fluid antenna system (FAS) is a novel technology that can switch its radiating element to different locations within a predefined space. By exploiting the natural fading of the signal envelope, FAS can select the best channel without complicated signal processing. This paper studies a power allocation problem in a FAS-assisted multi-user downlink system, where each user is equipped with a fluid antenna while the base station (BS) has multiple fixed-position antennas (FPAs). We investigate the sum rate maximization problem under power constraint using the weighted minimum mean squared error (WMMSE) method. Simulation results show that the achieved sum rate of fluid antenna is much higher than that of FPA.

articleTitle: Performance of Different Polar Code Decoding Over NOMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the performance of different polar decoding algorithms over an uplink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system. The polar code which has low complexity can be decoded in two ways: sequential decoding like successive cancellation (SC) and parallel decoding like belief propagation (BP). We further introduce their list versions: SC list (SCL), CRC-aided SC list (CA-SCL) and BP list (BPL) which have better error performance. Simulation results show that BP outperforms SC by 0.2 dB over Gaussian channel, and by 0.5 dB over Rayleigh fading channel. Meanwhile, SCL achieves performance gain of 0.2 dB over BPL in both channels. Moreover, latency analysis shows that BP can save 21.6% clock cycles (CCs) to SC and BPL can further achieve 47.7% CCs reduction compared to SCL and CA-SCL.

articleTitle: Parametric Modeling of a 5-order Waveguide Bandpass Filter Based on Neuro-TF Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced parametric mod-eling technique based on the Neuro-Tf approach and establishes a knowledge-based neural network (KBNN) model for a 5-order waveguide filter. The model takes the S-parameter of the electromagnetic (EM) simulation as the output and the geometric parameters of the filter as the input. By using the poles and residues of the transfer function as a knowledge rule, we accelerate the solving speed of nonlinear problems. This method performs better generalization than the traditional multi-layer perceptron (MLP) network model.

articleTitle: A Differential Oscillator Based on Filtering Power Divider With Low Phase Noise and Output Ports' Common-Mode Reflectionless Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a differential oscillator with low phase noise and output ports' common-mode reflectionless characteristics is presented. The proposed oscillator adopts a narrowband bandpass filtering power divider as the frequency selection network, simplifying the oscillator's design and improving the phase noise performance of the oscillator. A microstrip-slotline balun with common-mode reflectionless characteristics is utilized to accomplish the differential output and output ports' common-mode reflectionless performance. To validate the design method, the proposed oscillator's circuit is designed and simulated using the Advanced Design System software. The results show that the proposed differential oscillator has an output power of 6.987 dB, phase noise of-133.4 dBc/Hz @ 100 kHz and -155.3 dBc/Hz @ 1 MHz, second harmonic suppression of 65.289 dBc. Meanwhile, the common-mode reflectionless characteristic is achieved at the differential output ports, which verifies the proposed concept.

articleTitle: A Compact Tri-Band Antenna for WLAN and WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A compact tri-band antenna is proposed in this paper. The tri-band operation and bandwidth enhancement are achieved through the introduction of curved branches to a coplanar waveguide(CPW) fed monopole and L-shaped slots into the ground plane. Simulation results show that the lower band (2.32 - 2.58 GHz) of the proposed antenna covers the 2.4 GHz WLAN band, the middle band (3.38 - 3.81 GHz) covers the 3.5 GHz WiMAX band, and the upper band (4.39 - 6.93 GHz) covers the 5.2/5.8 GHz WLAN and 5.5 GHz WiMAX bands. Furthermore, the antenna is rather compact, with a size of only 0.21 ×0.28 × 0.01 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}^{3}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the freespace wavelength at the central frequency of the lower band.

articleTitle: Beamforming for a Highly Flexible Phased Array Conformed on a Shape-Variable Aperture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Flexible phased arrays have gained widespread attention in different areas. However, in practical applications, the arrays may conform on a shape-variable aperture, leading to real-time deformations. To maintain radiation performance, it is essential to achieve beamforming of the flexible phased array under arbitrary deformations. In this work, a phase-only update strategy is proposed to enable beam scanning for a two-dimensional flexible phased array under high deformations. Furthermore, a least squares-based strategy for simultaneous phase and amplitude updates is introduced to achieve simultaneous multi-beam forming for the flexible array under high deformations in real time. Finally, a 10 x 10 flexible array operating in the S-band is numerically simulated under typical bending deformations, validating the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed approaches.

articleTitle: An Efficient Joint Channel and Impulsive Noise Estimation Method Based on Variational Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) wireless communication systems, the joint estimation of channel and impulsive noise (IN) has become a research focus. The Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL) algorithm is widely adopted for this task due to its effectiveness in handling sparse signals. But, it suffers from high computational complexity and time-consuming iterations. To solve these issues, this paper proposes a Joint Channel and Impulsive Noise Estimation method based on Variational Autoencoders (JCIE-VAE). First, a lightweight encoder network structure is designed, where the joint vector composed of the channel and IN is treated as the latent variable in the VAE for estimation. This practice effectively reduced the computational complexity. Secondly, a learnable sparse prior distribution is introduced into the VAE, which allows simultaneous updates of both the prior and posterior distributions of the latent variable during training. As a result, the iterative process inherent in the SBL algorithm is avoided. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed JCIE-VAE method significantly reduces computation time. It improves estimation efficiency without compromising the bit error rate (BER).

articleTitle: Modeling of Electromagnetic Disturbance Characteristics of Bus Network Protocol Chip
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The study introduces a quantitative model that primarily endeavors to analyze and forecast the conducted emission behaviors of several archetypal digital devices. Through rigorous testing of the conducted emissions from representative digital chips, a model for the conducted emissions of digital integrated circuit chips is constructed, drawing upon the test outcomes. The Power Delivery Network model is acquired employing vector fitting techniques, whereas the chip's internal source model is deduced via indirect measurement methods. The comparative analysis reveals that the quantitative model's error margin remains within 3dB of the actual measured data, demonstrating its high degree of accuracy.

articleTitle: Phased Array Fed Reflector with Flexible Beam for High Throughput Satellite Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The phased array fed reflector antenna has the flexibility of scanning and shaping. Based on the conjugate field matching method, this paper studies the beam scanning performance of the reflector antenna under the condition of axial defocusing. With a 4.5m aperture and a focal to diameter ratio of 0.6, the reflector operating at 32GHz has good scanning performance within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \boldsymbol{10}^{\circ}$</tex>. The peak gain is 65.6dB and the gain is within 2.7dB. In addition, this paper also investigates the beamforming of the antenna to achieve different beamwidths under the same reflector aperture. The beam widths can change from 0.14 ° to 2.4 °, while the peak gain decreases from 62.5dBi to 40.7dBi.

articleTitle: Design of A Novel Frequency Selective Surface With Frequency Adjustable Fuctions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this letter, a novel frequency selective surface with frequency adjustable fuctions based on switchable transmission window is presented. The proposed structure consists of two metal layers and a dielectric layer, the transmission windows of four different tuning modes can be switched by controlling the state of varactor diodes. The simulation results show that this proposed structure offers a large tuning range (6.2GHz,~ l0.8GHz), the narrow band transmission characteristics are conducive to the needs of radar stealth.

articleTitle: A Ka Band Dual-Channel Amplitude And Phase Control Multi-Function Chip Based on GaAs E/D PHEMT Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a design approach for a novel 24–28 GHz dual-channel amplitude-phase control multi-function chip, which is constructed using the GaAs enhancement and depletion pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistor (E/D PHEMT) process. Each channel of the chip integrated a single-pole-double-throw (SPDT) switch, a digital phase shifter with 6 bits, a digital attenuator with 5 bits and a gain compensation amplifier. The measurement results show under a voltage of +5 V, the gain of the receiving channel is greater than 1 dB, the output power 1 dB compression (OP1dB) is greater than -2 dBm, and the current is 25 mA. The gain of the transmission channel is greater than 0.5 dB, the OP1dB is greater than 8.5 dBm, and the current is 40 mA. The root mean square error of the 64 state phase-shifting is less than 3 °, and 32 state attenuation root mean square error is less than 0.4 dB. The chip size is 6.2 mm × 5.0 mm. The proposed multi-function chip demonstrates high amplitude-phase control accuracy, small chip size, excellent performance and strong universality, which can be widely used in microwave transceiver modules.

articleTitle: An Efficient Parallel Subdomain DGFEM for Multi-Physics Coupling Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this work, a subdomain discontinuous Galerkin finite element method (DGFEM) is proposed for electromagnetic-thermal-stress analysis. The proposed DGFEM discretizes the second-order partial differential equations (PDEs) straightfor-wardly, and the domain decomposition property of DG method is simultaneously kept by introducing numerical flux and a suitable Robin transmission condition (RTC) at the interface of neighboring subdomains. With the aim to solve the decomposed problems in an efficient way, a finite-element tearing and interconnecting (FETI)-like procedure is applied to separate the unknowns into surface unknowns and volume unknowns. Besides, an effective MPI strategy is developed in order to solve the decomposed matrix equations pertinent to each subdomain in a parallel approach. Compared with the classic DG method, the proposed subdomain DGFEM not only largely decreases the unknowns, but also improves the efficiency significantly. Several examples are investigated by the proposed algorithm, which will be presented during the conference.

articleTitle: Neural Adaptive Video Streaming via Imitation Learning and Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive bitrate streaming (ABR) algorithm based on imitation learning and reinforcement learning, named BC-PPO ABR. Aiming at the problems of existing learning-based ABR algorithms, such as long training time and slow convergence, behavior cloning (BC) is introduced to make the policy network fit the expert strategy to achieve rapid convergence. Considering the severe network fluctuations caused by mmWave 5G, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm is incorporated into the training process of the policy network to limit the magnitude of updates between the old and new policies, thereby obtaining a stable and effective bitrate selection strategy. The experimental results show that BC-PPO ABR achieves better QoE compared to representative benchmark tests.

articleTitle: Research on Reconfigurable Fabry-Perot Beam Tilted Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A simple reconfigurable beam tilted antenna is designed based on Fabry-Perot structure in this paper. The reconfigurable characteristic is realized by properly designing the varactor diodes loaded partial reflective surface superstrate (PRS-Superstrate). The antenna could steer to 30-degree and 59-degree under the setting bias voltages. Simulation results also show that the antenna is with the good performance of high gain and low return loss at the working frequency.

articleTitle: Beam Optimization in Low Altitude Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper primarily analyzes the characteristics and issues of existing mobile wireless networks provided by telecom operators for low-altitude coverage, and explores construction and planning schemes for low-altitude wireless networks. It studies the low-altitude coverage capability of single base stations under different antenna types, scenarios, and beam configurations, with a focus on integrated air and terrestrial coverage. From the field test results, it is clear that existing ground networks can provide integrated air and terrestrial coverage with good effects. Moreover, this paper investigate feasible cluster schemes based on different beam optimization solutions that are both low-cost and high-performance, providing references for future low-altitude deployments by telecom operators.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Polarized Slot Antenna Array with Substrate-Integrated Coaxial Line Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel 5G-NR mm-Wave dual-polarized low-profile 4 × 4 antenna array using dual-mode substrate-integrated coaxial line (SICL) is proposed. By designing a mode converter using Γ-shaped feeding strip, this method achieves an integration of separated dual-polarized feeding networks into one feeding structure with high isolation. A stimulated isolation between two modes of the input port is higher than 21 dB over the overlapping bandwidth of 14% from 24 to 27.6 GHz covering the N258 band. The peak realized gain and radiation efficiency are 17.7 dBi and 94% for both horizontal and vertical polarization. The proposed antenna array has the advantages of simple feed, low profile and compact volume, showing significant potential in the next generation of wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Re-investigation of Coupled Microstrip Line for Crack Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The paper proposes a crack sensor based on the coupled microstrip line. Cracks alter the coupling coefficient, leading to a shift in the transmission zero of the isolation port. Simulation results demonstrate that the sensor is capable of detecting crack depth.

articleTitle: ESD Characterisation and Modelling of Digital Integrated Circuits Based on TLP Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper investigates the damage characteristics of digital integrated circuits under transmission line pulse (TLP) stress. Accurate damage data were obtained using TLP test. By analyzing the test results, we found that the same type of loops in the same digital integrated circuit have similar I-V characteristic curves and damage current values, while different types of loops have large differences. This indicates that the design of the electrostatic protection inside the chip has a significant effect on the ESD immunity of the loops. In order to more accurately simulate the loop characteristics of digital integrated circuits, this paper adopts a segmented linear modelling approach. The method is able to effectively consider the nonlinear characteristics of the loop, and the data validation proves that the simulation results are highly consistent with the measured data. The model provides a powerful theoretical support and tool for the design optimization, fault analysis and reliability assessment of digital integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Study on the Influence of Strong Electromagnetic Pulse on GaAs HEMT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: As a new generation of microwave and millimeter-wave devices, HEMTs have already become core components of microwave mixers, oscillators, and other such equipment. However, as integration levels continue to rise and device sizes shrink, microelectronic devices are becoming increasingly sensitive to various types of electromagnetic interference and thermal effects, which can cause damage. Therefore, it is necessary to study the damage effects and mechanisms of HEMT devices under electromagnetic interference. This research is conducted to address the issue that the core devices of radio frequency power amplifier integrated circuits are prone to interference or damage from strong electromagnetic pulses. It clarifies the interference or damage process of the core devices under the influence of strong electromagnetic pulses, establishes a GaAs HEMT device model under the coupling conditions of electricity, heat and magnetism, and analyzes the triggering process and failure mechanism. It investigates the impact of different electromagnetic parameters on the failure process, obtains the sensitive locations and parameters and establishes an interference model that can reflect different electromagnetic parameters. This research work provides a theoretical foundation for establishing and simulating the electromagnetic interference damage model of HEMT devices, and also accelerates research in related fields.

articleTitle: A Class-F23 VCO with Implicit Common-Mode Resonance Expansion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel harmonic-shaping Class-F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">23</inf> voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) with implicit common-mode (CM) resonance expansion. By adding single-ended capacitors to the gate node of the Gm transistors, the proposed VCO achieves common-mode resonance expansion. Implemented in a 65-nm CMOS process, the VCO achieves phase noise lower than -117.4 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset and figure-of-merit (FoM) higher than 189.6 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset over the entire tuning range.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly-Polarized Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna Array Using a Simplified 2×2 Subarray
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A wideband circularly-polarized (CP) cavity-backed slot antenna array using a simplified sub array is proposed in this paper. Two pairs of degenerate modes are excited in a single cavity, and each pair of degenerate modes is used to produce a CP band. A pair of metal prisms is utilized to allocate the two bands close to each other, and a wider AR bandwidth can be obtained. The radiating slots are excited by the electric field of the cavity modes, thus, 2×2 radiating cross-slots can be placed on the top wall so as to form a CP array with a simplified structure. Then, a 4×4 array is designed using the 2×2 subarray via a I-to-4 cavity-based power divider. Final simulation shows that the proposed 4×4 CP slot antenna array can achieve 16% bandwidth with a peak gain of 16.8 dBic and a peak total efficiency of 99.5%.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Implantable Antenna for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A compact dual-band dual-polarized implantable antenna is investigated in this study for bio-telemetry in biomedical applications. It operates in the wireless medical telemetry service band (1.395-1.432 GHz) with an impedance bandwidth of 1.22-1.69 GHz and in the industrial, scientific, and medical band (2.40-2.48 GHz) with an impedance bandwidth of 2.08-2.59 GHz. Besides, circular polarization is obtained in the upper band with 3-dB axial bandwidth of 2.22-2.50 GHz. Meandering technology is utilized to realize miniaturization and the dimensions of the antenna are optimized to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\times 6\times 0.4\text{ mm}^{3} (0.023 \times 0.028 \times 0.0019 {\lambda_{0}}^3, \lambda_0$</tex> is the wave length at 1.4 GHz) without introducing shorting-pins. Moreover, to better analyze the antenna tuning, equivalent circuits are constructed. Finally, for human safety, the specific absorption rate is analyzed.

articleTitle: A Linear Polarized Huygens Metasurface for Millimeter Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a low-profile, miniature, dual band, high gain metasurface with linear polarization. The proposed metasurface consists of two layers of rectangular metallic elements. Through sophisticated design of the element sizes and unit cell pitch, this metasurface effectively covers the 5G Frequency Range 2 (FR2) n257 and n258 bands with high gain. Simulation results demonstrate that the compact size and high-gain performance of the proposed design have significant potential for practical applications in vehicle borne communication.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Degree of Freedom of Holographic MIMO in Transformation Optics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Holographic multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication is made up of an ultra-dense array of antennas, whose channel models and potential applications are increasingly drawing attention. The capacity of MIMO systems has long been constrained by the aperture's limitations on degree of freedom (DOF) which has become a significant impediment to the development of holographic MIMO. Inspired by transformation optics, this paper proposed that the electromagnetic DOF can be invariant when the aperture is reduced. Based on the electromagnetic information theory, our work is aimed to exploring the potential to overcome the aperture-size limitation in MIMO antennas, offering an alternative path to enhance the DOF in 6G communication systems.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Omnidirectional Circular Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: To realize a wideband omnidirectional circular polarized antenna (OCPA), one omnidirectional antenna using polarizer and metasurface are designed, fabricated and measured. Omnidirectional circular polarized (CP) wave is achieved by the anisotropic dielectric polarizer. Then, the metasurface can compensate the phase difference of orthogonally polarized electromagnetic waves caused by the anisotropic dielectric polarizer as the frequency increasing. The phase difference can maintain in nearly 90° within a broad band. Hence, it can achieve wideband omnidirectional CP radiation. The measured results are consistent with the simulated ones. The measured results show that the proposed OCPA can achieve an impedance bandwidth of more than 70% (11 GHz-25 GHz) and an axial ration (AR) bandwidth of 66.6% (12 GHz - 24 GHz).

articleTitle: Planar Conical Beam Leaky-Wave Antenna with High Scanning Rate and Out-of-Roundness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This article introduces a method for generating a conical beam utilizing leaky-wave antenna (LWA) technology. By employing periodic concentric slots into the parallel plate waveguide, an omnidirectional conical beam leaky-wave antenna (CBLWA) with broad scanning capability is achieved. The proposed antenna comprises three primary components: a radiator layer, a matching layer, and a feeding layer. A one-toeight power divider is designed to feed the CBLWA at the center of the feeding layer. Due to the symmetry of the antenna structure, the cross-polarization is well suppressed over the entire operating band. The leaky-wave antenna operates within the frequency band of 30–37.3 GHz. The proposed antenna features a scanning angle of 46°, with a scanning rate of 2.1°/GHz across the operating band. Furthermore, the out-of-roundness (OoR) level is less than 2.2 dB, and the cross-polarization suppression is less than -25 dB. The characteristics of the proposed antenna, including its simple structure, high scanning rate, and effective cross-polarization suppression, make it a competitive choice for satellite communications and targeted area coverage.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band Low-Noise Amplifier Based on Transformer Matching Network in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A Ku-band two-stage low-noise amplifier (LNA) with transformer matching network is presented using 65-nm CMOS technology. The first stage employs transformer matching network to achieve a wide bandwidth. The second stage utilizes a triple-coupled transformer to enhance gain. The simulation results show that the proposed LNA achieves a peak gain (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) of 16 dB with a -3 dB bandwidth ranging from 10.7 to 20.7 GHz. The noise figure (NF) is between 3.28 and 3.92 dB, and the input 1-dB compression point (IP1dB) ranges from -19.6 to -17.1 dBm across the effective bandwidth. The input return loss (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) remains below -10 dB within the frequency range of 9.7 to 23.2 GHz. The LNA operates at a low power consumption of 3.8 mW, making it suitable for wideband applications.

articleTitle: A 39-GHz On-Chip Bandpass Filter using Coupled-Line Structure in 130-nm SiGe Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a design methodology is presented to generate transmission zeros (TZs) for a bandpass filter (BPF) at both lower and upper stopbands. As a result, the selectivity and the stopband suppression performance can be improved. Using this method, the TZs can be generated in a very flexible way. As proof of concept, a 39-GHz bandpass filter (BPF) is fabricated in 130-nm SiGe technology. Including the pad loss, the measured insertion loss is less than 3.5 dB, and the lower-stopband suppression is greater than 20 dB from DC to 31 GHz. Besides, the footprint, excluding the pads, is only 0.031 mm <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of a Wideband Dual-Polarized Printed-Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The performance of a broadband dual-polarized printed-dipole antenna has been significantly improved. Incorporating a parasitic element above the antenna has broadened its bandwidth to 63%, achieving a return loss exceeding 15 dB. Additionally, the bandwidth can be further expanded to 74% by incorporating an additional parasitic element. This extra element is able to be printed alongside the dipole and the integrated balun on one single substrate, while maintaining the antenna's simple design and facilitating easy manufacturing. The dual-polarized printed-dipole antennas, both with enhanced and further-enhanced bandwidths, demonstrate consistent radiation patterns and high isolation throughout their operational frequency ranges.

articleTitle: A Metasurface Based on Absorption and Phase Cancellation for RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a metasurface based on hybrid mechanism of absorption and phase cancellation is designed to achieve Radar Cross Section (RCS) reduction. Two types of the basic meta-atoms with absorption performance and a reflection phase difference of 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup> ± 37<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>are designed to achieve RCS reduction. The simulation results show that the -10 dB RCS reduction bandwidth of the metasurface is 130% (3.75 -17.75 GHz) and the -20 dB RCS reduction bandwidth of the metasurface is 103% (4.8 - 15 GHz). It does not contain lumped elements and has a compact structure with a profile height of 0.154 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>. What's more, the proposed metasurface is insensitive to oblique incidence and polarization.

articleTitle: A Multi-Antenna System for 6G/5G/4G Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Multi-antenna system is presented for 6G/5G/4G multi-mode mobile terminals. A low-profile dual-circularly polarized (CP) antenna is developed in S-band for 6G satellite mobile communications. The dual-CP antenna is realized based on two ±45° dipoles above an artificial reflector, which features a low antenna profile of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.03\lambda 0$</tex>. An 8-element MIMO antenna is integrated with the 6G dual-CP antenna for 5G terrestrial communications in the 3.5-GHz band. A broadband antenna is introduced in the 6G/5G antenna module for covering the 4G (or 2G/3G/4G) operating bands in 1.7-2.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Wide-Scan Tightly Coupled Dipole Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband, wide-scan tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) is designed. The dipole elements and integrated strip line balun are printed on a vertical printed circuit board (PCB) backed with a ground plane. The use of strip line balun can effectively broaden the bandwidth of antenna units and eliminate standing wave singularities within the working band. A wide-angle impedance matching (WAIM) layer printed with defective rings over the array aperture is used to achieve broadband and wide-angle scanning. The antenna is excited by a coaxial line with 50Ω characteristic impedance. Simulated results show that the design provides a 5:1 (from 2 GHz to 10 GHz) bandwidth while scanning to ±60° in E/H-plane, subject to VSWR < 3.

articleTitle: Digital Chip Susceptibility Assessment and Level Classification via the DPI Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: As the feature size of integrated circuits continues to shrink and the working environment becomes more complex and variable, their electromagnetic susceptibility directly affects the electromagnetic compatibility performance of the entire electronic device. This paper conducts a test and analysis of conducted electromagnetic susceptibility for digital integrated circuits based on the Direct Power Injection (DPI) method proposed in IEC 62132-4. The electromagnetic susceptibility levels of integrated circuits are systematically summarized, providing clear susceptibility judgment criteria for related experiments. A detailed assessment of the electromagnetic susceptibility of different pins of the same integrated circuit is carried out to comprehensively measure its overall anti-interference capability. A comparative analysis of the susceptibility threshold levels of integrated circuits is conducted. Through testing and analysis, it is found that digital power pins have stronger anti-interference capabilities compared to other functional pins, while output and reset control pins are more susceptible. In practical use environments, it is necessary to add necessary protection to ensure the normal operation of digital devices.

articleTitle: Integrated Design Method for Doherty Power Amplifier and Antenna Based on Lossy Equivalent Two-Port Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an integrated design method for Doherty power amplifier (DPA) and antenna based on lossy equivalent two-port network. The load modulation network in a traditional DPA and antenna is represented as a lossy two-port network. The input impedances of this network are adjusted to match the optimal impedances of both the carrier and auxiliary power amplifiers. By eliminating the separate matching network and the 50-ohm transmission line between the Doherty power amplifier and the antenna, this approach reduces the transmission loss and circuit size. The lossy two-port network is implemented by using a four-segment transmission line in combination with the antenna. The simulations show a saturation output power of 42.2 dBm, a saturation efficiency of 65%, and a 6 dB back-off efficiency of 51%. Additionally, it provides a small-signal gain of 12.3 dB with a gain compression of 0.7 dB at saturation.

articleTitle: A Terahertz Slab Photonic Crystal Circulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This study investigates a terahertz circulator based on slab photonic crystal. The slab circulator coupled to stander waveguide through a tapered slab structure. To further enhance impedance matching, a ridge structure is incorporated within the photonic crystal wave-guides. The circulator exhibits excellent transmission performance near the center frequency 0.225THz, achieving isolation is better than 20 dB, with insertion loss lower than 1 dB. These results demonstrate the potential of PC circulator for high-efficiency terahertz communication systems, offering low loss and strong isolation characteristics.

articleTitle: An UWB Monopole Antenna for Partial Discharge Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: An ultra-wideband (UWB) monopole antenna for partial discharge detection is proposed in this paper. The antenna is composed of a stepped monopole, a circular metal sleeve, an annular slot, a metal cap and a metal reflector. By using a 50 Ω coaxial cable to excite the monopole, good vertically polarized omnidirectional radiation performance is achieved for the monopole antenna. To improve the impedance matching, widen the impedance bandwidth and improve the gain of the proposed antenna, load a circular sleeve with a metal cap around the monopole. To further improve the impedance bandwidth of middle and low frequency bands, the monopole radiator is changed into a stepped monopole, and an annular slot is etched on the metal reflector. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna has an ultrawide impedance bandwidth of 102.6% for reflection coefficient S11 ≤ -10 dB, ranging from 1.69 GHz to 5.25 GHz. In addition, the antenna also has good omnidirectional radiation performance, and a gain range of 0.91 to 6.2 dBi. These performances show that the proposed antenna is highly competitive in partial discharge detection.

articleTitle: Research on Hotspot Heat Dissipation Characteristics of Chips Based on Parallel Microfluidic Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In order to explore the heat dissipation effect of the microfluidic channel, this paper designs a parallel microfluidic channel structure, tests its microfluidic channel heat dissipation performance, and explores the influence of the fluid inlet flow rate and hotspot location on the heat dissipation effect. The results show that adding this structure in the heat sink can significantly reduce the upper surface temperature, and the location of hotspots also has a big impact on the heat dissipation effect, indicating that the parallel microfluidic channel has a better heat dissipation performance.

articleTitle: All-Dielectric Air-Like Transparent Meta-Atoms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A perfect transparent object in free space should neither reflect nor refract under electromagnetic waves coming from arbitrary directions, regardless of shape and size. Therefore, metamaterials with air-like constitutive relations are required. The usual way of metamaterial design is to edit the composition of metallic rods and wires. Nevertheless, dielectrics are much more stable and less lossy than metals, which can be an alternative candidate to make metamaterials. In this paper, we propose a 3D all-dielectric example to render a nearly perfect transparent metaatom, which is composed of high-permittivity dielectric rather than metals. Detailed analysis shows that the macroscopic constitutive parameters of the object are identical to air by the dipole moment neutralization in its interior. Consequently, the designed structure behaves as the basic building block of a transparent object with arbitrary shape and size, which can be made by a simple stacking procedure. The effectiveness is validated through theoretical analysis and full-wave simulations. Due to the metal-free feature of our design, the proposed strategy is scalable to higher frequencies, i.e., terahertz and optical range. Thus, we envision that this approach can inspire some new applications, such as functional antenna radomes, ideal optical windows, and invisible obstacles.

articleTitle: A Compact LNA with Dual-Path Noise-Canceling and Gain Enhancement for 5G Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a compact low-noise-amplifier (LNA) employed dual-path noise-canceling and gain enhancement techniques. The LNA is composed of one cascode stage in combination with one common-source (CS) stage. The triple-coil transformer (TR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and dual-coil transformer (TR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) are used to provide noise-cancelling path and gain boosting. Implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS technology, the LNA consumes a DC power of 12 mW under a 1 V supply. The amplifier achieves a 16.7 dB peak gain with a 3-dB bandwidth from 25.2 GHz to 30.5 GHz. The optimum noise figure (NF) is 2.77 dB. The LNA occupies very compact chip area of only 0.08mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: An Integrated System Leveraging Inverse Scattering for Sensing and Backscatter Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we present an integrated system for sensing and backscatter communication using inverse scattering technique. This system enables simultaneous tag localization, identification, and communication in cluttered environments. Simulations demonstrate the system's ability to accurately identify tags individually and in combination while achieving concurrent backscatter communication.

articleTitle: Active IRS Aided Secure Design for Integrated Sensing and SWIPT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an active intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) assisted secure integrated sensing and simultaneous wireless information and power transfer system is proposed with the power splitting (PS) model adopted. Aiming to maximize the harvested power while satisfying the constraints of the integrated sidelobe level ratio and secrecy rate, an optimization problem is formulated to jointly determine the appropriate transmit beamforming, artificial noise (AN) vectors, PS ratios, as well as the amplification factors and phase shifts of the active IRS, which is non-convex and intractable. To overcome this challenge, we leverage semidefinite programming to transform it into a convex counterpart, and propose an alternating optimization algorithm to obtain a solution for the original problem. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme compared to benchmarks.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer
Author Keywords: simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Filtering Antenna Array for 4G/5G Base Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized miniaturized filtering antenna array designed for 4G and 5G multi-frequency applications. The proposed antenna array covers the 2.57-2.62 GHz (4G band 38) and 3.3-3.8 GHz (5G n78) frequency bands, achieving a peak in-band gain of 14.7 dBi. By incorporating parasitic structures, each antenna element exhibits effective filtering characteristics without extra filter circuit. The differential feeding and the filtering characteristics of the antenna elements together ensure that the array achieves a port isolation greater than 25 dB and cross-polarization levels below −25 dB. The antenna array maintains stable radiation patterns across the operating bands, making it a promising candidate for base station applications.

articleTitle: Power Analysis Method of Signal Components Based on Power Amplifier Behavior Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A method is proposed to analyze the power of the power amplifier (PA) output signal components. This method involves generating PA output signals using a memory polynomial (MP) model and then calculating the cross-correlation function of the PA input and output signals within the corresponding working bandwidth in the frequency domain. Finally, the spectrum of linear and nonlinear components can be obtained. To demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method, the PA output signal components is analyzed under constant/non-constant envelope signal stimulation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through comparative simulation and experiments.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Hard-Decision-Based ML Receiver for UsIM-SS Intra-Body Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Ultrasonic index modulation with spread spectrum (UsIM-SS) can achieve intra-body communications (IBCs) with high data rate and high reliability. However, existing maximum likelihood (ML) receivers, including soft-decision-based ML (S-ML) and hard-decision-based ML (H-ML), cannot provide a trade-off between complexity and reliability. To this end, this paper proposes an enhanced H-ML (E-H-ML) receiver for UsIM-SS. E- H - ML first estimates the received signal in each chip and uses the estimated chip signals to recover the modulation bits; then, the estimated modulation bits and estimated chip signals are jointly used to recover the index bits. The theoretical symbol error rate (SER) is derived and verified by Monte Carlo simulations, revealing that the proposed E- H - ML receiver can achieve lower SER than the H-ML receiver and much lower complexity than the S- ML receiver.

articleTitle: Electric Modulation of Extraordinary Optical Transmission Behavior Based on Graphene Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Metasurface is an ultrathin artificial composite composed of subwavelength unit structures according to a certain design arrangement, which plays a unique role in the field of electromagnetic waves modulation. As the first widely studied flat material, graphene consists of a monolayer of carbon atoms, which can effectively manipulate the operating band and function of the metasurface. Here, the authors propose and demonstrate a tunable electromagnetic extraordinary optical transmission (EOT) graphene metasurface. The metasurface consists of an aperture-double split ring resonator (A-DSRR), a dielectric and a graphene sandwich structure. The results show that EOT behavior can be realized by introducing the double split ring resonator (DSRR) into the aperture structure. In addition, it was found that the transmission amplitude of the graphene metasurface EOT behavior could be manipulated by reducing the sheet resistance of graphene from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{3000}\ \boldsymbol{\Omega}/\mathbf{sq}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{300}\ \boldsymbol{\Omega}/\mathbf{sq}$</tex>. The proposed EOT graphene metasurface design principle is promising for many applications of active electromagnetic control or optical modulation.

articleTitle: A Low-profile Ultra-Wideband Wide-Angle Scan Dual-Polarization Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband dual-polarized banyan tree antenna (BTA) is designed and manufactured aim to the requirements of the radar, communication, electronic warfare multifunctional integration system. The antenna is simulated and optimized by commercial electromagnetic simulation software with two-dimensional master-slave boundary. The operating frequency band is 2-6GHz and the scanning range is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex> in total space. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16\times 16$</tex> array prototype is fabricated. The active- VSWR measured results of the antenna at 2-6GHz are blew 2.7. The antenna could scan 45° without grating lobe, and the cross-polarization is below -20 dB.

articleTitle: Degration Behavior and Mechanism Analysis of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs After RF Overdrive Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This work mainly observes the degradation behavior and analyses mechanism of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs under RF (Radio Frequency) overdrive stress. According to experiment results, after long-term RF stress of up to 650 hours, DC characteristics emerged degradation phenomenon. For example, the decrease of output drain current was up to 180 mA, threshold voltage had a positive drift of 0.23V and gate leakage current decreased one orders of magnitude. Gate-Lag and low frequency noise testing revealed an increase in defect in the device, and these traps capture electrons, which leads to more depletion of two dimensional electron gas (2DEG) in the channel. The increase in trap density can be explained by the hot electron effect under RF stress. The experimental results can provide reference for the reliability study of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs.

articleTitle: Bandwidth and Radiation Performance Improvement Technique for Electrically Small Antennas Based on a Negative-Resistance Parametric Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative bandwidth and radiation performance improvement technique tailored for electrically small antennas. To enhance bandwidth, the Bode-Fano theorem is employed in conjunction with a magnetic electrically small antenna, which serves as a high-Q resonator. The theorem provides insights into the maximum received signal level for a specified bandwidth. Additionally, a negative-resistance parametric amplifier is seamlessly integrated into the structure as an active component, effectively compensating for the mismatch loss introduced by the Bode-Fano theorem while maintaining optimal radiation performance.

articleTitle: Spurious-Free SAW Resonators Using Lithium Tantalate on Silicon Carbide Substrate with Rhomboidal Apodization IDT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: With the rapid development of 5G communication technology, the performance of surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators using hetero-layered structure urgently needs to be further improved. For instance, the transverse modes can significantly reduce the performance of SAW devices. Herein, a strategy by employing rhomboidal apodization interdigital-transducer (IDT) was proposed to suppress the spurious modes, and thus spurious-free 42° <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y$</tex>-cut <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{LiTaO}_{3}/\text{SiO}_{2}/\alpha-\text{Si}/\text{SiC}$</tex> SAW resonators were successfully implemented. The experiment results have verified the successful suppression of transverse modes when the rhomboidal apodization IDT is adopted. The resonant frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_\mathrm{r})$</tex> of fabricated SAW resonators is around 1 GHz. Moreover, the SAW resonator with normal IDTs exhibits a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k_{\mathrm{e}\mathrm{f}\mathrm{f}}^{2}$</tex> of 11.4% and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Bode}-Q_{\max}$</tex> of 2160. The resonator with rhomboidal apodization IDTs exhibits a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k_{\mathrm{e}\mathrm{f}\mathrm{f}}^{2}$</tex> of 10.9%, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Bode}-Q_{\max}$</tex> of 2185 and the transverse mode has been suppressed.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization for STAR-RIS Aided Non-Line-of-Sight ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) technology has gained prominence in wireless communication by integrating data transmission and sensing functionalities within wireless networks. This paper introduces a novel strategy for optimizing the performance of non-line-of-sight ISAC systems. The optimization problem is equivalently transformed by the weighted minimum mean square error model of the received signal, and we propose a five-stage hybrid optimization algorithm based on block coordinate descent (BCD) to solve this problem, which converts the problem into a convex form. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed five-stage hybrid BCD optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Varactor-Tunable Frequency Selective Surface with Excellent Angular Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band varactor-tunable bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) with angular stability is proposed. The FSS comprises composite multi-resonance metallic structure where varactors are mounted symmetrically and bias network etched on the opposite side of the dielectric substrate, achieving dual passbands with independent tunability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FSS exhibits continuous operating frequency from 2.4 to 5.75 GHz and from 5.7 to 9.63 GHz by controlling the bias voltage applied to the corresponding varactors. Moreover, it maintains angular stability for incident angles up to 75° under both TE and TM electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: A Decoupling Method for Tightly Coupled Dual-Polarized Filtenna with Restored Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the fact that a single decoupling method cannot address all types of coupling at the same time, this paper presents a decoupling method that can be used for tightly coupled dual-polarized filtenna arrays. The method employs partially reflective surfaces (PRSs) and semi-transmissive non-resonant square ring baffles to achieve the suppression of co-polarization and cross-polarization couplings, respectively. They are both composed of a periodic arrangement of sub-units printed with simple metal strips, and good decoupling can be achieved without careful design. In order to verify the decoupling effect of this method in the filtenna, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 3$</tex> dual-polarized array antennas with a close distance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.37\lambda_{0}$</tex> are implemented. The simulation results show that the isolation of the co-polarization and cross-polarization ports improves from 12 dB and 10 dB, respectively, to more than 18 dB, while the return loss in the antenna's operating band remains below −10 dB. Compared with the reference array without decoupling measures, the radiation pattern of the array has no distortion, and the cross-polarization ratio in the boresight direction is improved by more than 9.3 dB, achieving the restoration of radiation patterns and the enhancement of peakrealized gain. The above results indicate that the decoupling method has a promising application in BSG/6G massive MIMO tightly coupled arrays.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Energy-Selective Surface Design for High-Power Microwave Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: An ultra-wideband energy selective surface (ESS) is proposed and simulated, which consists of a PIN diode and a cross-metal bar grid, which utilizes the switching characteristics of the diode to achieve protection against high-power microwaves. An equivalent circuit model (ECM) is also established to simulate the performance of this structure for comparison with the full-wave simulation. The simulation results illustrate that when the diode is on, the ESS is in the protection state and can reflect high-power microwaves in the 0-7.36 GHz band with a shielding efficiency (SE) greater than 10 dB; when the diode is off, the ESS is in the wave-transparent state, it can pass low-power signals with low insertion loss (IL) in the 3.42 GHz-6.7 GHz band, and the IL is less than 1 dB. The ESS demonstrates robust stability in response to changes in incident angle and polarization, enabling the provision of ultra-wideband protection.

articleTitle: Simulation-Inserted Optimization of Sixth-Pole Waveguide Filter With Quasi-Newton Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Recently, a novel electromagnetic (EM) optimization method, called as Simulation-inserted optimization (SIO), utilizes the finite element method (FEM) to solve the EM response. In the SIO technique, quasi-Newton method is introduced to accelerate the optimization processes. The SIO technique with quasi-Newton method outperforms other gradient-based optimization methods, including the SIO with Newton's method. This paper seeks to apply the SIO technique with quasi-Newton method to design a sixth-pole filter with two transmission zeros.

articleTitle: A L Band High-Efficiency GaN Power Tube Based on the Large Signal Scaling Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a high-efficiency power tube operating in L-band is designed by the 0.35μm gate length and 28V GaN HEMT process die developed by Nanjing Electronic Devices Institute and the AlGaN/GaN scalable large signal model simulation guidance. The power tube is designed by a single GaN die with a total gate width of 14.4mm using a hybrid integrated internal matching scheme. The drain voltage is 28V and the frequency band is 1100~1400 MHz. The simulated result show that the saturated output power of the power tube is greater than 46 dBm and the power additional efficiency can reach up to 70% in the operating frequency band, which is highly consistent with the test data. The power tube has a very broad engineering application prospect.

articleTitle: Front-to-Back Ratio Enhancement of a Base-Station Antenna with a Smaller Reflector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The front-to-back ratio (FBR) of a dual-polarized antenna is proposed and enhanced for 5G new radio (NR) base-station. To improve the performance of FBR, a slotted metal rim is incorporated. Moreover, the inclusion of a metal ring and a parasitic hat increases the gain of the antenna. The reflector is smaller, featuring a dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.46\lambda_{\mathrm{L}}\times 0.46\lambda_{\mathrm{L},}$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\mathrm{L}}$</tex> represents wavelength in the free-space at the minimum operational frequency. Within the 5G frequency bands n28, n82, and n83, which span from 0.69 to 0.96 GHz, the antenna achieves the FBR exceeding 25 dB under the condition of return loss more than 15 dB. In addition, it provides a gain exceeding 7 dBi and ensures an isolation level greater than 30 dB.

articleTitle: A Broadband LNA with Tri-Coupled Transformer for Gm-Boosting and Noise Canceling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband lower noise amplify (LNA) in 40nm process to support 5G wireless communication. The LNA cascades two differential neutralized common-source (CS) stages. Using tri-coupled transformer to achieve noise cancel, Gm boosting and broadband matching can be achieved concurrently. Moreover, the current refuse and nonlinear capacitance compensation techniques are employed to reduce power consumption and enhance linearity. The simulation results show that the LNA achieves a peak gain of 16.54 dB with a 3 dB bandwidth from 17.9 to 32.1 GHz. The minimum NF is 2.61 dB at 25.2 GHz and is below 4 dB from 17.9 to 32.1GHz. The overall size of the compact LNA is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.09\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. The IP1dB is -5.42 dB with a power consumption of 11mw.

articleTitle: Simulation Verification on OTA Characteristics of Surface Wave Propagation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A simulation of the OTA (Over The Air) characteristics of the proposed surface wave propagation system is verified in this paper. The system is designed on a reconfigurable porous surface where cavities are evenly distributed and can be filled with metal posts on demand. To guide the wave to the desired positions, a transmission channel employing two rows of metallic posts is created. While at the desirable position, a specially designed surface wave launcher can launch the wave into free space from the surface to the users. As shown in the simulated results, the attenuation of waves propagating on the surface is much lower than that in the free space, the proposed system can be utilized as a position-flexible radiator as described in fluid antenna systems (FAS). The simulated OTA performance of the system shows excellent characteristics of low propagation loss and high propagation efficiency, making it a good candidate for sixth generation (6G) mobile communications.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of High Efficiency CMOS RF Class-D Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The practical power-added-efficiency (PAE) of class-D RF power amplifier (PA) deviates from the theoretical value 100% greatly because of some inevitable non-ideal effects. This paper proposes three design considerations to improve the performance of class-D RF PA. Based on those design considerations, two pieces of class-D RF PA, powered by 1.8V and 3.3V supply respectively, have been implemented by standard CMOS 0.18um process. With 800MHz stimulus, measurement results show that the PAE and output power reach 42% and 10.5dBm for 1.8V supply part, 38% and 15.4dBm for 3.3V supply part, which demonstrates the practicability of the introduced design considerations.

articleTitle: A Fast Computer-Aided Method for Filter Design Based on Vector Fitting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Traditional filter design methods heavily rely on electromagnetic (EM) simulations and a trial-and-error process, resulting in low efficiency. These methods fail to provide clear optimization directions under predefined filter topologies and performance specifications, leading to increased computational resource consumption. To address this issue, we propose a fast computer-aided design method based on vector fitting. This method de-embeds and fits the S-parameters of the filter to accurately extract and optimize the coupling matrix, significantly simplifying the design and optimization process.
