Furthermore, it provides clear optimization targets, reducing design complexity and improving optimization efficiency. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a high-temperature superconducting filter, which presents significant tuning challenges, is used as an example. The results demonstrate that this method significantly enhances the efficiency of filter design and optimization while reducing the design difficulty.

articleTitle: A Vertically Polarized Tapered Monopole Antenna with Reconfigurable Patterns for WiFi Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This article presents a compact vertically polarized tapered monopole antenna with pattern reconfigurable capability for WiFi applications. The antenna is based on the Yagi-Uda principle, and achieves reconfigurable patterns by switching the states of the PIN diodes connected to the passive stubs. In addition, in order to improve the bandwidth of the antenna, the tapered monopole is properly designed, which can cover the WiFi band (5.15-5.85 GHz) well. Simulation results show that the peak gain of the proposed antenna is 7.3dBi, and the radiation efficiency is stable. Due to the simple structure and good radiation characteristics, it is suitable for WiFi indoor applications.

articleTitle: A Compact and High-Efficiency Class-F Voltage Doubler Rectifier for Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel class-F voltage doubler rectifier is proposed for radio frequency energy harvesting (RFEH). In the proposed structure, two different harmonic termination networks are employed to block the harmonics of voltage doubler diodes and reshape current waveform and voltage waveform. Thus, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the conventional voltage doubler rectifier can be improved significantly. For validation, a prototype is fabricated and measured. The measured peak PCE is 76.5% with a 13 dBm input power and a 1600 Ω load. Besides, the input power range for PCE high than 50% is from 1.8 to 15.5 dBm.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Lightweight Neural Network for Massive MIMO CSI Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, channel state information (CSI) is usually estimated and fed back to the BS from the user equipment (UE), and the quality of CSI received by the BS has a large impact on the performance of the large-scale MIMO system. To address the problem that existing DL-based CSI feedback methods have difficulty in balancing model complexity and feedback performance, in this work, we propose CFNet, an efficient and lightweight model based on MetaFormer, which employs convolution to replace the attention module in the traditional Transformer model. CFNet combines the lightweight of convolutional neural networks with the high performance of the Vision Transformer (VIT) model. CFNet combines the lightweight of convolutional neural network and the high performance of Vision Transformer (VIT) model. Experimental results show that CFNet can maintain high feedback accuracy with very low computational complexity under different compression ratios.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Antenna with Integrated Low-Pass Filtering for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel dual-functional device that integrates a dual-polarized filtering antenna and a lowpass filter, specifically designed for base station applications. The proposed device operates as an antenna with a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 1.68-1.89 GHz, covering the 5G n3 band. It achieves a maximum in-band gain of 9.05 dBi and a radiation efficiency exceeding 93%, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex> dual polarization, which is crucial for base station operations. Additionally, the integrated filtering circuit provides more than 20 dB out-of-band rejection in the lower frequency band and over 15 dB in the upper frequency band, thanks to a parasitic patch introducing a radiation null at 2.12 GHz. As a low-pass filter, the device exhibits a cutoff frequency of 0.96 GHz, with an in-band insertion loss of less than 0.36 dB and stopband suppression exceeding 20 dB. This dualfunctional device can be cascaded with another antenna element operating at frequencies below 0.96 GHz, eliminating the need for additional filtering circuits, thereby significantly saving space and making it an excellent candidate for base station applications.

articleTitle: A 5-35 GHz Broadband LNA Using Cascode Structure and RLC Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband low-noise amplifier (LNA) that operates across the 5–35 GHz frequency range is presented, which is implemented using both cascode and common-source structures combined with RLC feedback technique. The cascode structure in the first two stages provides sufficient gain while reducing the bandwidth limitations caused by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{C_{gd}}$</tex>, The introduction of peaking inductors and source degeneration inductors mitigate the effects of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{C_{ds}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{C_{gs}}$</tex>, respectively. The third stage is a Common Source Amplifier, where the feedback is controlled by adjusting the RLC network to enhance high-frequency gain, achieving broadband performance. The proposed broadband LNA has been validated by a 0.1-μm GaAs pHEMT technology. It delivers an average gain of 31 dB across a 3 dB bandwidth of 5 GHz to 35 GHz, while maintaining a minimum noise figure (NF) of 1.56 dB.

articleTitle: A Posteriori Error Estimation in Computational Electromagnetics: A Recovery-Based Error Indicator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Recently, goal-oriented error estimation methods and mesh adaptation have garnered attention within the electromagnetic community. However, these methods are constrained by Galerkin orthogonality, necessitating that at least one of either the primal or dual problem achieves high-order estimation. Current approaches tend to be either computationally expensive or struggle to provide an accurate measure of the absolute error. In contrast, the method proposed in this paper enables a posteriori error estimation without incurring additional computational costs, and it ensures that the absolute error size remains within an acceptable range, by a recovery-based error indicator.

articleTitle: Coupled Feed Mechanically Rotating Antenna for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Direction-Finding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a coupled feed mechanically rotating antenna for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) direction-finding (DF). The propeller blades themselves are designed as a half-wave dipole., with a cross-shaped feed component mounted on the blade safety cover. Capacitive coupling is used to feed the dipole without direct contact. When the propeller rotates., the mechanical movement guides the figure-eight radiation pattern to rotate within the horizontal plane, allowing a single-channel amplitude receiver to achieve direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. Simulation and numerical experiment results demonstrate that this antenna maintains DF accuracy comparable to traditional mechanically rotating dipoles, while offering the advantages of lower cost and reduced payload. Compared to the direct feeding method for rotating propeller antenna, the coupled feeding approach better fits the mechanical and dynamic structure of the UAV and offers higher efficiency and achievable gain.

articleTitle: A Periodic Leaky-Wave Antenna Based on Double Stubs Structure for Open Stopband Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A periodic leaky-wave antenna based on double stubs structure for open stopband (OSB) suppression is investigated. The antenna is made up of six uniform units, each of which consists of double stubs structure. The simulation results demonstrate that this antenna exhibits excellent performance in suppressing OSB in the broadside direction. Within the frequency range of 6.3-11.2 GHz, a seamless beam scanning capability spanning from -58° to +55° is achieved, featuring a maximum gain level of 14.0 dBi.

articleTitle: A CMOS RF Front-End for E-Band FMCW Phased-Array Radar Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The proposed front-end is fully integrated, included a phase shifter (PS), a driver amplifier (DA) and a power amplifier (PA). In order to improve the phase resolution, a capacitorfree and inductance-compensated quadrature generator circuit (QGC) is proposed in PS for excellent I/Q signals. Besides, the peak gain and bandwidth of the PS are improved about 20% and 30% with a series peaking inductance, respectively. To verify the effectiveness of the methods above, a RF front-end chip is designed and manufactured in 40-nm CMOS. According to the measurement result, a bandwidth of 69.8-78.5 GHz and 6-bit phase shifting resolution with the RMS phase error of 3.2-3.5 deg are achieved. The power consumption is 154 mW under 1.1 V. The output P1dB (OP1dB) of 11.6 dBm and the saturated output power (Psat) of 14 dBm at 74.5 GHz is measured which can meet a range over 200 meters. This front-end is suitable for E-band FMCW phased-array radar transmitter, due to a high phase resolution and a long detection distance.

articleTitle: A Low-Altitude Network Base Station Planning Model Based on PPO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The rapid development of low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has led to significant communication demands. Leveraging cellular networks to support low-altitude UAV communication offers cost advantages. However, existing cellular networks suffer from inadequate aerial coverage and the complexity of urban terrestrial channels. To address these challenges, we propose a novel low-altitude network base station planning model based on the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. Our approach involves calculating the low-altitude coverage capabilities of different base station types using ray tracing techniques. We construct a decision model for base station placement and utilize the PPO algorithm to determine optimal base station configurations. Through reinforcement learning training and simulation validation, we demonstrate that our model effectively generates base station deployment plans, achieving predefined signal coverage objectives.

articleTitle: A Stable Time-Domain Electric Field Integral Equation Discretized with a Truncated Multistep Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The convolution quadrature (CQ) method represents as a prevalent time-domain integral equation (TDIE) equation for perfect electric conductor (PEC) scattering problems due to its notable stability. However, the global sequence derived from the CQ method entails significant memory consumption. In this paper, we embrace a truncated version of the CQ method, which selectively truncates based on the varying threshold values of vector and scalar potential components. This approach minimizes the memory usage and reduces the calculation for impedance matrices greatly. Furthermore, a numerical example validates the accuracy of our proposed method. It is also demonstrated the feasibility of the truncation technique, with a balance between its efficiency and accuracy achieved.

Author Keywords: Time domain electric field integral equation (TDEFIE)

articleTitle: An Inverse Class-F Circularly Polarized Active Integrated Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an inverse Class-F circularly polarized (CP) active integrated antenna is proposed. In the design, a Lshaped slot is etched in the radiating patch, which achieves circular polarization for the antenna. Subsequently, a defected ground structure (DGS) and two T-shaped slits are introduced in the CP antenna to suppress the second and third harmonics, which make the antenna an inverse Class-F load. Finally, the proposed CP antenna is directly integrated with the power amplifier (PA), which allows the PA to operate in the inverse Class-F mode, thus improving the power-added efficiency (PAE) of the PA. The inverse Class-F AIA can obtain a PAE of 73.01% and an output power of 41 dBm at 2.45 GHz.

articleTitle: A Compact Base Station Antenna Based on Ungrounded Radiator and Capacitive Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this letter, a novel miniaturization method for base station antennas based on ungrounded radiator and capacitive compensation is introduced. The miniaturization is achieved by loading a slot on the radiating structure of the dipole antenna to provide a capacitive component, thereby neutralizing the inductive component introduced by the ungrounded radiator. To broaden the bandwidth, a coupling layer, consisting of a printed square ring and a square patch, is introduced as a parasitic element above the antenna, inducing a new parasitic mode. In addition, the bandwidth is extended by enhancing the coupling between two pairs of dipole antennas through a downward extension of the radiator. The results reveal that the proposed compact antenna achieves a -10 dB bandwidth of 1.742.2 GHz (23.4%) with a radiator size of only 0.13 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{L}^{2}$</tex> and a profile of 0.209 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{L}(\lambda_{L}$</tex> is the wavelength at the lowest frequency).

articleTitle: Fast Beam Steering and High Gain 1 X 4 End-Fired Phased-Array Antenna Based on Liquid Crystal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: An end-fired phased-array antenna with millisecond fast beam steering is proposed based on liquid crystal (LC). The proposed phased-array antenna is constructed by a feeding network, transition structures, LC-based phase shifters, and Yagi-Uda antennas. Distinguished from the reported LCbased phased-arrays, the proposed one incorporates the LC display technology-implemented phase shifter with a waveguide feeding network. To achieve millisecond fast beam steering, the LC thickness in the phase shifter is configured as 4 µm since the beam steering time of the antenna is proportional to the square of the LC thickness. The air-filled waveguide benefits from low losses, leading to reduced insertion loss in the feeding network. The reflection coefficients remain below -10 dB within the frequency range of 13.8 GHz to 15.4 GHz, and the maximum gain is 5.56 dBi at 14.25 GHz.

articleTitle: A High-Isolation Dual-Circularly-Polarized Antenna for Simultaneous Transmit and Receive Based on the Differential-Mode and Common-Mode Coupling Cancellation Principle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an improved co-aperture, dual circularly polarized (CP) microstrip patch antenna with good isolation for simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) applications is proposed. The antenna consists of a slot-loaded cross-shaped patch with four slots embedded around the patch to adjust impedance matching and a rectangular slot in the center of the patch to achieve dual CP. In addition, the transmitting (Tx) to receiving (Rx) isolation of the antenna is improved through the differential-mode and common-mode coupling cancellation theory. Simulation results show that the final antenna has compact overall dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.43\lambda \times 1.43\lambda \times 0.033\lambda$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> is the guided wavelength at the center frequency. The antenna operates over a bandwidth of 4.21 GHz-4.32 GHz with isolation higher than 15 dB and up to 33 dB. At the same time, it has a consistent radiation pattern. Compared with similar antennas, this antenna has the characteristics of small aperture size and a simpler feeding structure, which is suitable for STAR systems.

articleTitle: Measurement and Modeling on THz Channels in Urban Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The realization of high-rate terahertz (THz) communication necessitates comprehensive channel studies across various typical scenarios. This work focuses on THz channel characteristics in urban environments, a representative outdoor communication setting. We employ a ray tracing algorithm to plan propagation routes and conduct channel measurements in a real urban scenario, adhering to the planned incidence angles. Our analysis encompasses the variations in scattering and absorption losses under swept-frequency measurements. Leveraging surface sensing properties, we derive the dielectric constant of urban structures at 220 GHz. This information facilitates the development of a THz channel model, enabling path loss calculations for diverse propagation paths. We further investigate path loss differences under various weather conditions, including rainfall and snowfall. The study examines the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at 220 GHz, performs distribution fitting, and analyzes bit error rates to elucidate the distinctive characteristics of THz channels in urban scenarios. This comprehensive approach provides crucial insights for the design and optimization of THz communication systems in city environments.

articleTitle: Conformal Leaky-Wave Antenna with Scanning Beam Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a conformal leaky-wave antenna with scanning beam based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs). By utilizing the SSPPs to slow-wave propagation, the rectangular patch units distributed on two staggered layers are used as the radiating structure, and the scanning beam of the conformal leaky-wave antenna is achieved by controlling the on/off state of the PIN diodes on the units. Through simulation analysis, it is found that the antenna operates in the frequency band of 4.2 GHz to 5.5 GHz, and at the frequency of 5.4 GHz, it can achieve beam scanning at multiple angles in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi$</tex> direction at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta=90^{\circ}$</tex>, with a side lobe level lower than -5dB and a realized gain of around 10dBi. The conformal antenna is suitable for operation on curved surfaces such as cylinders.

articleTitle: CDiB-IDS: Contextual DistilBERT-Based Intrusion Detection System for IoV
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: With the rise of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), cyber-security risks have become increasingly prominent. We propose an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) utilizing the DistilBERT model, which efficiently recognizes complex network behavior patterns. This system translates network traffic into sequences for enhanced contextual analysis, improving detection accuracy. DistilBERT's reduced encoding layers enhance the IDS model's performance. Our framework demonstrates effectiveness on the Car-Hacking and CICIDS2018 datasets, achieving an F1 score of 100% on the Car-Hacking dataset and at least a 1.28% improvement over other models on the CICIDS2018 dataset.

articleTitle: A Terahertz Fully Metallic Frequency-Scanning Leaky-Wave Antenna with Low Elevation Coverage and High Beam Scanning Rate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A terahertz fully metallic frequency-scanning leaky-wave antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna primarily consists of a novel one-dimensional sliding symmetrical spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) transmission line and staggered periodic modulation structure. Compared with traditional fully metallic SSPP transmission lines, the proposed fully metallic sliding symmetrical SSPP transmission line displays higher dispersion and low elevation coverage potential. The Open-Stopband (OSB) effect is suppressed by loading a periodic modulation structure with staggered arrangement on both sides. The simulation results show that the beam scanning range from - 78.5° to +26.5° is achieved in the band from 175 GHz to 220 GHz, with the beam scanning rate of 460.8°% and peak gain from 6.4 dBi to 11.7 dBi. The low elevation coverage and high beam scanning rate are realized.

articleTitle: Delay Error Correction Method of Photonic Beamforming Array Antenna Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Photonic beamforming array antenna addresses the problem of beam squint in the traditional pure electric phase shifter. However, in practical applications, time delay errors can arise from factors such as manufacturing defects, optical fiber variations, and temperature changes. In this study, a photonic beamforming array antenna model is established. During the experiment, systematic error for the delay of each element is introduced into the array. This kind of error has a significant impact on the performance of array antenna. Based on the technology of machine learning(ML), a method for delay error correction of photonic beamforming array antenna is proposed. The results has demonstrated that the accuracy of the beam direction is significantly improved. The time delay systematic error in optical fiber delay lines are corrected, the overall performance of the photonic beamforming array antenna system is improved.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna Array for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) microstrip patch antenna array with a sequential phase feeding network is proposed for low earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems. The antenna array has a bandwidth of 12.7% from 27.3 GHz to 31 GHz with a peak gain of 11.6 dBic. The feeding network is sequentially phased with a quadrature phase shift. The antenna array has advantages such as stable gain, small size, ability to form arrays, and ability to scan at large angles. The proposed antenna array has been used for low earth orbit satellite communication in the GW program frequency band, covering its 27.5-31 GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: Analysis and Testing of Conducted Electromagnetic Susceptibility in Integrated Circuits Based on Multi-Waveform Interference Using BCI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper integrates a Bulk Current Injection (BCI) probe with various types of interference signals to design a multi-waveform interference-based BCI conducted electromagnetic susceptibility (EMS) test for integrated circuits. This paper analyzes the impact of different types of interference signals on the susceptibility of integrated circuits according to the results of conducted electromagnetic susceptibility testing.

articleTitle: Fast RCS Estimation of Chaff Clouds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a method-of-moments (MoM) based solver for the fast estimation of chaff cloud scattering properties. The solver is designed using the method of moments, where uniformly distributed spherical chaff clouds are decomposed into blocks, with block size dependent on the wavelength. By employing optimized strategies for impedance matrix filling and generating an initial guess for the algebraic solution, the computational time is significantly reduced. Ultimately, the proposed method achieves a large reduction in computation time, while maintaining the accuracy of RCS calculations.

articleTitle: Shaped Beam Synthesis Using Bayesian Optimization-Based Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: The shaped beam synthesis of array antenna is known as a computional-cost task. In this article, a bayesian optimization (BO)-based convolutional neural network (CNN) is proposed for shaped beam synthesis (SBS). By establishing BO-CNN framework, the shaped beam pattern is synthesized in real-time without the array geometry limits. The CNN is composed of convolutional layers and fully-connected layers. The former is served as an extractor to extract the features, while the latter predicts the array excitation using the extracted the features in real-time. However, during the training of CNN, many architecture hyper-parameters of CNN need to be tuned by experience. In the proposed algorithm, by introducing the BO into the CNN, the automatic design of the CNN can easily achieved and the CNN performance is further improved. The effectiveness of the BO-CNN is validated by two examples, and its performance is compared with that of the convex optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: 1-Bit Coding Beam Scanning Antenna with Parasitic Patch
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this article, a 1-bit coding reconfigurable beam scanning antenna is proposed. A symmetry of the feeding network is utilized to achieve 1-bit phase conversion. This element is combined with parasitic patch, air gap and uses the method of slot couplings to increase the antenna's bandwidth. The array has a relative bandwidth of 29% from 3.6 to 4.9 GHz. Simulated result indicates that the proposed array can cover the beam scanning range from −49° to 49° without grating lobe.

articleTitle: Design of New Small Broadband Two-Dimensional Sum-Difference Integrated Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A novel two-dimensional sum-difference network (TDSDN) based on branch line coupler and 90° phase shifter is proposed in this paper, which overcomes the shortcomings of traditional sum-difference networks and exhibits wider bandwidth. The fractional impedance bandwidth for |S11|<-10dB is 36% at a center frequency of 5.5 GHz, along with a phase shift of approximately ±8° in operating band.

articleTitle: An Energy Selective Surface With Ultra- Broadband Absorption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Energy Selective Surface (ESS) designed for electromagnetic protection within its operating band and broadband absorption outside. Full-wave simulation results show that under low-power signal conditions, the ESS produces a passband at 2.8 GHz with an Insertion Loss (IL) of 0.9 dB, and the relative bandwidth of the absorption band reaches 95%. Under high-power signal conditions, the diodes on the ESS are activated, converting the passband into a stopband, with a shielding effectiveness (SE) of up to 17 dB at 2.8 GHz. Within the range of 0.5 GHz to 13.4 GHz, the SE remains above 10 dB. The absorption band remains stable under high-power signals, indicating that the designed absorption band is unaffected by the input power level. The ESS also exhibits oblique incidence stability, enhancing its practical applicability. The research contributes to the advancement of ESS technology for electromagnetic protection and compatibility in diverse environments.

articleTitle: Channel Characterization for China Lunar Base at 500 MHz and 23 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A lunar base is a pivotal platform for future human exploration and utilization of the Moon. This study examines the channel characteristics of the 500 MHz and 23 GHz frequency bands within a future lunar base. Utilizing ray tracing technology combined with empirical modeling methods and based on the “cloverleaf” lunar base layout, simulations and analyses were conducted on the channel performance within working, living, and biological cabins. Results indicate that at 500 MHz, signals exhibit superior penetration and anti-interference capabilities, whereas 23 GHz signals are significantly affected by multipath effects and environmental factors. The channel characteristics vary notably among different cabins, with the biological cabin experiencing the most complex propagation environment. The findings provide essential guidance for developing efficient and secure communication systems for future lunar bases.

articleTitle: A T-Shaped Feed Single-Band Miniaturized Antenna Suitable for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A miniaturized single-band antenna element suitable for 5G applications is proposed. The proposed antenna element innovatively integrates a T-shaped feed structure with a compact meandered loop radiating element. It features two resonant points at 3.4 GHz and 3.55 GHz, with the overlapping resonant bands exhibiting a wide -6dB impedance bandwidth of 360 MHz (3.27 GHz-3.63 GHz), fully meeting the application requirements of the 3300 MHz to 3600 MHz band. Additionally, the efficiency of the antenna element is approximately 50-68%. The work also presents results such as the antenna S-parameters, voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR), current distribution, and far-field radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Design Strategy for RCS Reduction of Metasurfaces Considering Inter-Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Based on the principle of multiphase cancellation, a checkerboard metasurface was designed to reduce the radar cross section (RCS). Each meta-atom in the metasurface features a sandwich structure comprising ring-shaped metal patches of varying sizes, dielectric substrates (FR4) of different thicknesses, and metal ground planes, arranged from top to bottom. Initially, the GA was employed to optimize the meta-atoms, ensuring that their phase response across the frequency band covers the broadest possible angular range. Subsequently, based on the combination of PSO and GA (GA-PSO), optimize the scattering fields of the metasurface across various frequencies, polarizations, and incident angles, aiming to achieve significant RCS reduction. The proposed metasurface demonstrated a 10 dB RCS reduction within the frequency range of 4–40 GHz for normal incident angle. Finally, samples were fabricated and measured, with experimental results showing good agreement with simulation predictions.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Dielectric Resonator 2-D Beam Scanning Phased Array Antenna Based on Liquid Crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized dielectric resonator two-dimensional (2-D) beam scanning phased-array antenna with liquid crystal (LC) -based spiral delay line is proposed in this paper. The structure, which is designed at 20 GHz, consists of a 4 × 4 elliptically shaped dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array, continuously spiral delay lines and radio frequency (RF) feeding line. Elliptically shaped DRA and sequential rotation (SR) are used to achieve both wide impedance and axial ratio (AR) bandwidths. The proposed phased array exhibits an impedance bandwidth of 38% (16.75– 24.62 GHz) and 3-dB AR bandwidth of 20% (18–22 GHz). The beam scanning range is ±30° in both ϕ = 0°and ϕ = 90°planes. The proposed phased array antenna has advantages of wide impedance bandwidth and wide AR bandwidth, which has potential application value in satellite communication.

articleTitle: Pulse Compression Using Chirped Delay Line
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This article proposes a method of compressing highfrequency electromagnetic pulses using chirped delay lines. By applying a novel pre-distortion to the input signal and inputting it into a reflective chirped delay line for matched filtering, the peak amplitude can achieve a gain of over 6 dB. And the pulse duration can be compressed to 1/10 of the original pulse width. Compared to using waveguide type dispersion delay lines, this scheme can effectively reduce the system volume.

articleTitle: Beam Modulation on 1-Bit Transmissive Reconfigurable Metasurface in C-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A 1-bit transmissive active metasurface unit is designed. Two PIN diodes are always in opposite states, so that the X-polarized waves correspond to symmetrical structures in two different states. Moreover, the feed network is designed in order to make the X-polarized waves produce different electromagnetic responses when passing through the metasurface. The symmetrical structure makes the metasurface element form a phase difference of 180 degrees while the transmission coefficient remains almost unchanged, and the transmission coefficient is over 0.7 in the band of 5–7 GHZ. 17% relative bandwidth is achieved in the C-band Besides, simulation software is used to verify the beam control capability of the metasurface array, which realizes the nearfield focusing function of the translational focus at 6.1GHz.

articleTitle: A Filtering Quadrature Coupler with Ultra-Wide Stopband
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a 90° filtering quadrature coupler with ultra-wide upper stopband. It consists of four parallel coupled feeding lines with enhanced coupling strength and a circular patch. The filtering response is achieved by the coupled feeding lines. To improve the out-of-band suppression level, two types of open stubs are utilized at the end of the coupled-line section. A slot is introduced at the center of the circular patch to realize equal power division. For demonstration, a filtering coupler operating at 4 GHz is designed, fabricated and measured. A 18 dB out-of-band suppression level ranged from 5 to 19 GHz is realized.

articleTitle: Remote Monitoring System for Communication Devices on Cloud Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: An additional remote monitoring system on the cloud platform without changing existing communication devices is proposed. The system continuously monitors communication devices and can quickly detect any malfunctions in the communication devices. This allows us to reduce the number of on-site inspections and better control costs. This remote monitoring system mainly includes data collection terminals, communication networks and cloud platforms. The data collection terminal does not change the structure of the device. It achieves online remote monitoring of the operation status of communication devices by connecting to the cloud platform.

articleTitle: Dual Circularly Polarized Shared-Aperture Phased Array Antenna for K/Ka-Band Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-frequency shared-aperture phased array antenna designed for K/Ka-band satellite applications. The low-band (LB) antenna is superimposed on the high-band (HB) antenna, with a slot structure allowing the high-frequency signals to pass through the upper patch. The circular polarization is achieved by employing the dual-feed methods. The two array antennas can achieve scanning ranges of ±45° and ±50°, respectively, with an axial ratio below 3dB. The proposed phased array system can be a candidate for K/Ka-band satellite applications.

articleTitle: A Self-Decoupling Circularly Polarized MIMO Microstrip Patch Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A self-decoupling circularly polarized (CP) multi-input multi-output (MIMO) microstrip patch antenna (MPA) array is proposed. The array comprises two identical square microstrip patch antennas (MPAs) and each patch is excited by a coaxial cable through an L-shaped microstrip line. Moreover, two corners are etched on the patch for CP radiation. It has been found that by appropriately selecting the length of the L-shaped microstrip line, CP radiation can be generated in the active MPA, and linearly polarized (LP) radiation can be obtained in the passive MPA, thus realizing polarization mismatch. On the other hand, a null-field region can be obtained in the coupled MPA. By placing the feeding probe of the coupled MPA in the null-field region, no energy can reach the port. Therefore, a high port isolation of more than 47 dB can be realized between the driven antenna and passive antenna, without requiring additional decoupling structure.

articleTitle: A Simplification Method of 3-D Aeroengine Model for BCI Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Advancements in commercial electromagnetic simulation software alongside affordable computational hardware now empower researchers to successfully conduct intricate electromagnetic simulations. However, in the field of aviation industry, the computational cost can be still unaffordable due to the complexity of electromagnetic simulation. Therefore, reduction of computational cost has become a research hotspot for which simplification of simulation model is one of the effective ways. The simplified simulation will be compared to the original simulation to ensure that the calculated result does not vary significantly due to the absence of experimental conditions. In this paper, lightning strike on an aeroengine is simulated by bulk current injection (BCI), the induced current and EM field of controller are analyzed. A simplification method of geometric structure, of which the reliability is guaranteed by contrast verification, is proposed for the electromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: Dual-Band MIMO Antenna With Circular Polarization in WBAN Band for Metal-Frame Smartwatches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: A multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna operating in the dual bands of 2.40-GHz wireless local area network (WLAN) and 5.80-GHz wireless body area network (WBAN), is presented for metal-frame smartwatches. An L-shaped closed slot is etched on the ground as the antenna element. Then, an open slot is added to the element, introducing capacitive loading in the upper band. By adjusting the open slot, the element achieves circular polarization in WBAN band. Finally, the two elements are placed symmetrically around the ground diagonal with cutting decoupling slots. When the proposed antenna was worn on the wrist, the maximum simulated -6-dB impedance bandwidths are 29.0% (2.11-2.82 GHz) and 31.9% (4.48-6.33 GHz) with the isolations of greater than 15.5 dB and 15.2 dB in WLAN and WBAN bands, respectively. Additionally, the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth ranges from 5.68 to 6.03 GHz. The dimensions of the antenna are 0.318×0.318×0.041 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>(at 2.45 GHz).

articleTitle: Mm-Wave Wide-/Dual-Band Filtering Antennas Based on Multinull Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Millimeter-wave wideband/dual-band filtering antennas are presented based on a multinull resonator, which comprises of a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity- backed slot. In wideband design, the multinull resonator provides three radiation nulls, resulting in high frequency selectivity with a rectangular coefficient K = 1.16 at bandedges (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}=\Delta \mathrm{f}_{-20\text{dB}}/\Delta \mathrm{f}_{-3\text{dB}}$</tex>). Four resonate modes including TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">120</inf>, a slot mode, a patch mode, and a strip mode are merged together, obtaining a wide bandwidth of 31%, a high gain of 10.4 dBi, and stable radiation patterns. A prototype of the wideband design was fabricated and measured. The multinull resonator can also be used in dual-band design. It provides two resonant modes and three radiation nulls. With a modified patch radiator, a dual- bandfiltering response with two modes and two radiation nulls for each band is realized.

articleTitle: Lunar Surface Scattering Simulation Based on an Automatic Matching Algorithm From Optical Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: Research on lunar often requires the combination of multi-sensor images, which requires an image-to-image alignment. In fact, the result of the alignment will directly affect the subsequent research and the analysis of the results. In this paper, we match optical and multi-sensor images based on image matching techniques. Thus, it is possible to combine Digital Elevation Model (DEM) and Synthetic Aperture radar (SAR) data. Our method uses a Gabor-Wavelet filter for texture extraction and Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC) for matching the extracted texture. And the best matching parameters are obtained when the NCC value is maximized. In addition, this work combines SAR data and DEM data through image matching, and applies the results to imaging simulation.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Faulty-Free Antenna Pattern in the Presence of Fault Elements of a Transmitarray in Planar-Near-Field-Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an effective source reconstruction method for planar near-field-measurement-based diagnosis. The proposed method uses spatial convolution to extrapolate the two planar far fields under the two frequency points, where one is the over-sampled low-frequency far field, the other is the under-sampled high-frequency far field. Based on the progressive similarity theory, the two far fields are highly similar and the under-sampled one at high frequency can be assimilated by the over-sampled one at low frequency. In this regard, the Kmeans clustering and Voronoi diagram are used to realize the data assimilation, and the reconstructed far field is then back projected onto the extreme near-field plane by the deconvolution method. Finally, the far-field pattern can be obtained by the near-to-far-field transformation algorithm, having good accuracy compared with the simulated one. More importantly, the proposed method can save the acquisition time significantly and improve the efficiency of the diagnosis measurement system.

articleTitle: Security Enhancing for IRS-Aided NOMA Networks via Constructive Interference Precoding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 10th International Symposium on Microwave, Antenna, Propagation and EMC Technologies for Wireless Communications (MAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a constructive interference precoding (CIP) enabled secure intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheme, lever-aging both the inter-user interference and artificial noise to boost the legitimate transmission of far user, while inducing the eavesdropper to decode the deceptive information. Based on this CIP-NOMA scheme, we minimize the transmit power under the perfect channel state information (CSI), subject to the CIP constraint for the far user and eavesdropper, while guaranteeing the quality of service and successive interference cancellation for the near user and the IRS unit modulus constraint. To handle this non-convex problem, an alternating optimization algorithm is proposed. Specifically, by alternately optimizing the precoding vectors at the base station and the IRS reflecting matrix via the successive convex approximation and the penalty-based algorithm, respectively, a reliable solution can be obtained. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can achieve better security performance with less energy consumption compared to the conventional NOMA.
